# Roadmap

Living list of work items beyond the current state, with enough context per entry that any one of them could be picked up as a self-contained chunk. Priority order is *suggested*, not strict.

Each entry has the same shape: a one-line summary, a *why* (the user-visible payoff), a *what* (load-bearing technical detail), and any *gotchas / open questions* known going in.

---

## How to use this doc

When starting a new chunk in Claude Code:

1. Pick an item from "Next up". Earlier items have more context inheritance.
2. Open the relevant section in the prompt: *"Read CLAUDE.md and docs/dev/roadmap.md section 1 (Schema-change planning helper). Propose a design before writing code."*
3. Iterate on the plan.
4. Implement.
5. Update this file when the chunk lands — move the entry to "Recently landed" and trim it to one line.

**Row-level filtering — per-table `--where` predicate ([ADR-0173](../adr/adr-0173-row-level-where-filter.md), filed 2026-07-17 from an operator request).** The missing filter granularity below namespace (`--include/exclude-database`/`-schema`), table (`--include/exclude-table`), and value (`--redact`): `--where TABLE=<predicate>` (native source SQL, source-keyed, repeatable — mirrors `backfill --where` + pscale `--wheres`). Use case: extract only the rows matching criteria (users in certain countries/regions, a per-tenant carve-out, a GDPR-scoped or staging-subset extract) and send just those to the destination. **BOTH PHASES SHIPPED 2026-07-17** (in released tags v0.99.276+). **Phase 1 (migrate) — SHIPPED (`cde284b8`)** — pushes the predicate into the source read (`buildSelect` → `SELECT … WHERE <chunk_bounds> AND (<predicate>)`, composed with the keyset chunker + the ADR-0076 pool), threads it into `verify`, and handles the load-bearing FK-orphan gotcha (filtering a parent → 23503 on the target) via a loud coded refusal (`SLUICE-E-WHERE-FK-ORPHAN`) + the existing `--allow-degraded-fks`; referential-aware auto-parent-inclusion (the pg_dump `--table`/Jailer subsetting problem) deferred as a harder follow-on. **Phase 2 (continuous *filtered* sync) — SHIPPED (`b4f929da`; a real operator use case met the demand-gate)** — client-side per-change eval over a restricted, faithfully-evaluable predicate grammar (`internal/rowpredicate`; refuses functions/subqueries/ordering/ci-collation-string/tz-temporal loudly so client-eval can't diverge from source-eval), the row-move-in/out dispatch (INSERT on move-in, DELETE on move-out), a full-before-image preflight (`SLUICE-E-WHERE-CDC-BEFORE-IMAGE`: `binlog_row_image=FULL`/`REPLICA IDENTITY FULL`), and a single-sourced snapshot↔CDC predicate. **The row-move-OUT "killer" surfaced live** — the readers narrow the before-image to the PK, so the filtered column was absent at eval → fixed by a zero-value-safe `SetFullBeforeImageTables` reader opt-out (full before-image for filtered tables, re-narrow before apply). **Phase 3 (ADR-0174, SHIPPED v0.99.278) — continuous `sync --where` now WORKS on MySQL-family / Vitess / VStream sources** (it was refused): faithful collation-aware client-side eval reusing Vitess's own `evalengine.NullsafeCompare` lifted the ci/ai-collation refusal (`8655b27c`), and the predicate is pushed server-side into the VStream filter (`9d89cd7c`). Follow-on hardening v0.99.279–283: PAD-SPACE/UCA/MariaDB-`_nopad_` collation faithfulness, the **A0 PAD-SPACE client-copy fallback** (`a702725b`, v0.99.283 — the NO-PAD VStream server filter can't reduce a PAD-SPACE column, so it streams unfiltered server-side and filters client-side), ENUM-under-collation (M1-5), FLOAT ordering as float64 + the single-precision-FLOAT-ordering refusal on the A0 fallback (SL1), and the M2-2 vindex-safety result (a `--where` on a primary vindex column is safe — Vitess refuses in-place vindex UPDATE). **Follow-ons:** the "filtered/subset migration" guide **SHIPPED v0.99.277** (`docs/operator/filtered-subset-migration.md`, with FK-orphan handling folded in); referential-aware auto-parent-inclusion (pg_dump/Jailer subsetting) remains the harder deferred follow-on.

**Postgres publication scope isolation ([ADR-0175](../adr/adr-0175-postgres-publication-scope-isolation.md)) — ✅ SHIPPED v0.99.287.** A **silent-loss** shape reachable by a reasonable operator sequence. The PG replication *slot* is per-stream and overridable (`--slot-name`, whose help text advertises running concurrent instances against one source), but the *publication* — `pgoutput`'s table filter, sent per stream as a `START_REPLICATION` plugin arg — is a hardcoded `defaultPublication = "sluice_pub"` with **no flag, config key, env var, or DSN parameter**, and no name argument on `EnsurePublication`/`AddPublicationTables`. Cold start runs `ALTER PUBLICATION sluice_pub SET TABLE <this stream's tables>`, which replaces the table set atomically, so a second concurrent PG-source stream with a **disjoint `--include-table` scope silently de-scopes the first**: its slot stays healthy and keeps advancing (nothing binds a publication to a slot — `cdc_reader.go:2176`), `pgoutput` emits nothing for its tables, and `sync status`/`sync health` report a current stream. Warm resume never re-asserts scope, so restarting the starved stream doesn't repair it. Safe today only because the one shipped multi-stream PG shape — the ADR-0122 fleet cold-start — shares an identical scope; **staged/"wave" migration is the natural way an operator reaches the unguarded case** (see `docs/operator/staged-wave-migration.md`, which currently routes operators around it). **Shipped:** (1) the load-bearing half — refuses the clobber: before a `SET TABLE` / `FOR ALL TABLES`-recreate that would *remove* tables, probe `pg_replication_slots` for other **active** `sluice\_%` slots and refuse with a new `SLUICE-E-CDC-PUBLICATION-SCOPE-CONFLICT`; widening/equal scopes and the additive `schema add-table` path never fire, so no shipped shape changes behavior; (2) `--publication-name` mirroring `--slot-name` (same `sluice_` prefix convention, default unchanged so upgrades aren't breaking), threaded via a `WithPublication` copy-and-return option like the existing `WithConnectionLabel`. **Gate (Tier 1) BUILT:** `internal/pipeline/publication_scope_conflict_pg_integration_test.go` — two concurrent PG-source streamers with disjoint scopes, asserting both targets receive their own changes, plus a refusal pin and a widening-must-not-fire pin. VERIFIED NON-VACUOUS: run against deliberately-disabled fix code it fails at exactly the starvation assertion ("wave A stopped receiving changes after wave B cold-started"), while the widening pin passes even pre-fix. **Residual/follow-up — ✅ CLOSED — SHIPPED v0.99.289 (existence semantics):** the guard's conflict signal is now slot EXISTENCE, not activity — a slot is the durable source-side claim that a stream holds a scope and intends to resume, so the "momentarily inactive slot" window is gone (pinned by `TestPublicationScope_InactiveSlotStillConflicts`); the binding-registry alternative is recorded as REJECTED in the ADR (source-side table = permission-gated guard that weakens exactly where it matters). Per-stream publications as a default remain the ADR-0176 prerequisite chunk (see that ADR's ratchet plan), not an ADR-0175 item. **Amended 2026-07-21:** the guard keys on the whole publication *definition* (tables + per-table attributes), not the table set, since PG 15+ row filters would otherwise reproduce the clobber one level down (identical table sets, differing predicates); per-stream publications are the recorded direction of travel.

**PG 15+ publication features — surveyed 2026-07-21 (prompted by the Supabase `etl` project's PG 15+ recommendation).** sluice uses **none** of the three today: `formatPublicationTableList` (`cdc_reader.go:2437`) emits bare qualified identifiers, and `pg_publication_namespace` is only *read* (in `publicationIsEmpty`), never written. Version floor is not a blocker — the test matrix is `postgres:16` (dominant), 17, 18, 19, and `serverVersionNum` gating already exists. Dispositions: **(a) row filters → [ADR-0176](../adr/adr-0176-pg-publication-row-filter-pushdown.md), ✅ IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-23 (chunk 2, released v0.99.290)** — server-side push-down for PG-source `sync --where`, the analogue of ADR-0174 Piece 2. Shipped inside a proven envelope per the ADR's A0 discipline: the conservative `pgPushdownEligible` classifier (pinned change-detector envelope), the single-sourced `WHERE (<pred>)` rendering in `formatPublicationTableList` gated on PG 15+, the `ir.PublicationRowFilterer` seam, client-side eval retained as the equivalence belt, the real-PG-16 per-cell oracle (`TestPublicationScope_PushdownOracle`, ~41 cells, zero divergent cells found), and the transactional no-op probe that lets a filtered stream's cold restart re-assert its own filter without false-refusing against peer slots. See the ADR's Status block for the shipped surface. **(b) column lists → [ADR-0177](../adr/adr-0177-pg-publication-column-lists.md), DISCOVERY, no adoption** — no sluice surface to implement it (we filter at namespace/table/row/value, not column); `--redact` is the *opposite* feature, not the fit. Revisit only with a concrete use case + a designed `--include/exclude-column` contract + ADR-0175. **(c) `FOR TABLES IN SCHEMA`** — unchanged: stays the already-filed WAL-volume optimisation the multi-schema CDC path notes at `cdc_reader.go:2244` (`FOR ALL TABLES` + reader-side `inScope` remains the correctness boundary); revisit on a multi-schema decode-volume complaint.

**Column-DEFAULT changes are silently NOT forwarded mid-sync — confirmed gap, CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, design of record = [ADR-0179](../adr/adr-0179-pg-ddl-catalog-capture-logical-messages.md) (2026-07-21, corrected 2026-07-22).** Surfaced by comparing sluice's DDL forwarding against the Supabase `etl` announcement's list (add / remove / rename column, nullability, **defaults**). sluice covers the first four via `ir.AlterAddColumn` / `AlterDropColumn` / `AlterRenameColumn` / `AlterColumnType` / `AlterColumnNullability` (ADR-0091, default-on) — but a `SET DEFAULT` is *silently skipped*: `diffAlteredColumn` (`shard_consolidation_probe.go`) compares only `Type` and `Nullable`, so a default-only delta yields `classes == 0` → `ShapeKindNone` → the intercept's no-op pass-through. **Severity — be precise:** NOT silent data loss (CDC carries explicit row values, so replicated rows are fine) and `sluice schema diff` DOES detect the drift (`ExpectedDefault`/`ActualDefault`/`DefaultLowConfidence`, `ir/diff/schema_diff.go`). It bites **at cutover**: once the app writes to the target, an INSERT omitting the column gets the *stale* default. The tenets-relevant part is the *silence* — `ShapeKindNone` asserts "nothing changed" when something did.

**⛔ THE OBVIOUS FIX DOES NOT WORK — implemented 2026-07-22, then REVERTED. Do not retry it.** Adding `Default` to `diffAlteredColumn` + a `ShapeKindAlterColumnDefault` + an `AlterColumnDefault` applier is simultaneously **dangerous and ineffective**, because **pgoutput's `Relation` message carries no defaults at all**: the PG CDC path projects via `projectRelation(rel)` into a `relationColumn{Name, OID, TypeMod, Type, KeyColumn}` — there is no `Default` field because the wire message has none. So (1) at the **seed→CDC boundary** the `pre` (full `SchemaReader` catalog read, real defaults) vs `post` (pgoutput, nil defaults) comparison classifies EVERY column-bearing table as a default change and emits **`DROP DEFAULT`**, destroying the target's defaults on the first boundary of every sync; and (2) at CDC→CDC boundaries both sides are nil, so a real `SET DEFAULT` is *still* never detected. Same trap as **Bug 83** (pgoutput also omits `attnotnull`, which is why the PG writer force-sets `Nullable=true` on forwarded ADD COLUMN). Corroborating evidence was already in-tree: `schema_forward_engage.go`'s `defaultProber` queries the SOURCE for a column's canonical default precisely because the CDC IR's defaults are empty. MySQL is the same from the other side — its forward-path IR is the binlog table map + a type/nullability signature read, no `Default` anywhere in its CDC reader. **Generalisable lesson: a shape classifier can only classify what the change stream actually carries — before extending the shape catalog with a new column attribute, confirm that attribute survives into the CDC-projected IR on every source that would use it.**

**The known-correct mechanism (supabase/etl, read at commit `6d21f3f`): push the catalog INTO the WAL.** They hit the same wall — that is *why* their machinery exists — and did NOT use a client-side probe. `crates/etl/migrations/source/20260415100000_schema_change_messages.up.sql` installs a **DDL event trigger** (`on ddl_command_end when tag in ('ALTER TABLE')`) whose function reads `pg_attribute` ⋈ `pg_attrdef` (`pg_get_expr(ad.adbin, ad.adrelid)`), builds a JSONB catalog snapshot (`attname`/`atttypid`/`atttypmod`/`attnotnull`/`atthasdef`/`default_expression`/`attidentity`/`atthasmissing`) and emits it **in-band** via `pg_logical_emit_message(true, 'supabase_etl_ddl', …)` — the leading `true` (TRANSACTIONAL) being the load-bearing bit. Their own comment: the function *"intentionally avoids PL/pgSQL EXCEPTION handlers to keep `pg_logical_emit_message()` in the top-level transaction and preserve the expected ordering of DDL messages relative to relation and DML events."* The consumer decodes it as a logical-replication `Message` and feeds the SAME `build_table_schema` used for bootstrap, so the two paths cannot drift. **A client-side catalog probe is explicitly REJECTED** (ADR-0179): it needs no privilege but **cannot be ordered** — by probe time the source may have moved on, and the observed state has no position in the change stream.

**Disposition: NOT building it now; the gap stays documented.** The blocker is that `CREATE EVENT TRIGGER` needs **superuser** (or a platform-granted equivalent like `rds_superuser`) — Supabase can install it because they own the platform (their `etl-api` even has explicit event-trigger drop logic for teardown), whereas sluice targets a wide managed-provider matrix. So it could never be the default PG path; it would be an **opt-in capability with a loud refusal** where the privilege is absent, and a change to the slot-based engine's "a publication and a slot, nothing else" contract (precedent exists in the `pgtrigger`/`sqlite-trigger`/`d1-trigger` family + `docs/database-objects.md`). **If it is ever costed, cost it as "PG DDL fidelity", not "the default gap"** — the same payload carries `attnotnull` (closing Bug 83's compensation) and `attidentity`, so one mechanism closes several gaps and the return is materially better. Full design, the rejected alternatives, and the test plan are in ADR-0179.

**Analytical / warehouse destinations (BigQuery et al.) — DEMAND-GATED, not started (surveyed 2026-07-21).** Prompted by the Supabase Pipelines alpha listing BigQuery as a destination. **Assessment: this is a new target *class*, not a new engine**, and the IR is the easy part. All 13 registered engines today are OLTP or file-based; a warehouse target breaks three core contracts: (1) `ChangeApplier` assumes **idempotent upsert** (ADR-0010, `INSERT … ON CONFLICT`) and BigQuery has no primary keys, no unique enforcement, no `ON CONFLICT`; (2) the streaming path (**Storage Write API**) is **append-only** while `UPDATE`/`DELETE`/`MERGE` are quota-limited DML — the standard CDC-to-warehouse pattern is *append change events to a staging table, then periodically MERGE*, a different **orchestration model**, not a different writer; (3) **position commit** (ADR-0007) writes the CDC position *in the same transaction as the data* — BigQuery has no equivalent cross-statement transaction, so the exactly-once story would rest on Storage Write API stream offsets, a wholly different mechanism. **The GCP head start is smaller than it looks:** `go.mod` carries `cloud.google.com/go/kms` (direct, backup encryption) and `cloud.google.com/go/storage` (indirect, via gocloud `gcsblob` for `gs://` backup targets) — auth/credential plumbing carries over, but there is **no BigQuery client anywhere**. **Interim path that already works:** `backup export-as-parquet` (ADR-0164) + `gs://` blob targets → BigQuery external table / load job — a well-trodden route needing ~zero new sluice code, and parquet already has an independent-reader CI gate (DuckDB). **Next step if demand appears: validate parquet → GCS → BigQuery end to end and publish it as a cookbook recipe** alongside `duckdb-on-sluice-backups.md` — hours of work, exercises real GCP credentials, and tests demand *before* committing to a second target contract. A native streaming BigQuery target should not start until that recipe shows traction; per the tenets, zero users means validating the existing surface outranks a new vertical. **The design sketch, if demand ever arrives, is [ADR-0178](../adr/adr-0178-analytical-target-class-changesink.md)** — `ir.ChangeSink` as a sibling contract to `ChangeApplier` (derived-not-stored position frontier, at-least-once-append + dedup-at-merge with an optional exactly-once offset capability, `append` vs `merged` materialization modes, ADD-COLUMN-only schema evolution). It **composes with** the parquet path rather than replacing it: parquet→GCS→load job as the initial load, ChangeSink for the CDC leg. Read it before anyone starts writing a `RowWriter` for a warehouse — "add a BigQuery engine" is the wrong mental model and an expensive thing to discover mid-implementation.

**SQLite CHECK-constraint `IN` support — ✅ FIXED + SHIPPED v0.99.287; pins now GREEN and un-skipped.** Surfaced by reviewing [planetscale/cli#1299](https://github.com/planetscale/cli/pull/1299) against sluice. **Ground truth beat the code-reading prediction — record what actually happens, not what was expected.** The prediction was "PG rejects `boolean = integer` in the DEFERRED constraint phase, after the copy." Wrong. sluice refuses **at create-tables**, before any data moves: `pipeline: create tables: table "flags": refuse loudly: CHECK constraint "" carries a non-portable SQLite expression "is_in IN (0, 1)" with no provably-equivalent Postgres translation`. So the guard is better-placed than assumed (no long-migration-then-fail), but the impact is worse in a different way: **the migration is blocked outright.** Two ORDERED gaps:

- **Gap A (the blocker, NO type-inference involvement) — `internal/translate/sqlite_expr.go` has no `IN` node.** Its node set is verbatim / string / ident / binary / unary / isNull / concat / func / cast. `col IN (0,1)` is portable to PG *and* MySQL **verbatim**, but it cannot be parsed, so it falls to the catch-all non-portable refusal. Since SQLite has no BOOLEAN type, `INTEGER CHECK (x IN (0,1))` is *the* canonical boolean idiom — so **any SQLite/D1 database using it cannot be migrated at all** without the operator first dropping its CHECK constraints. This is over-refusal on a provably-safe expression, and it is the piece blocking real migrations today.
- **Gap B (PlanetScale's actual fix, reachable only AFTER A) — boolean-coercion-aware CHECK rewriting.** Once `IN` parses, a column that `--infer-types` promotes to PG `BOOLEAN` needs its CHECK rewritten to boolean literals: `IN (0,1)` → `IN (false,true)`, `= 1` → `= true`, plus `<>` / `!=` / reversed operand order (`1 = col`). Without it the CHECK emits as syntactically valid SQL that PG then rejects (`operator does not exist: boolean = integer`) — which is where the original prediction *thought* we already were. Non-coerced columns must be left untouched (`plain_count IN (0,1,2)` stays integer).

**Also in scope (same pass, same file family): the strftime() DEFAULT translation set.** `translateSQLiteDefaultExpr` (`internal/engines/postgres/ddl_default_sqlite.go`) recognises only `datetime('now')`/`date('now')`/`time('now')` + the `CURRENT_*` spellings; every `strftime(...)` form falls to the loud-WARN **DROP** path, so the migration succeeds but the DEFAULT is absent on the target and a DEFAULT-omitting INSERT after cutover gets NULL. Safe but lossy. planetscale/cli#1299's set is worth borrowing: `strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ','now')` → `date_trunc('second', now())`; `%s` on a numeric column → `extract(epoch from ...)`; the safe-modifier family (`±N day/hour/minute/second/month/year`, `start of day/month/year`, timezone no-ops); unknown patterns keep today's fallback.

**Pins are WRITTEN and CONFIRMED FAILING** — `internal/pipeline/migrate_infer_types_check_default_cross_integration_test.go`, covering every operator shape (`IN` / `=` / `<>` / `!=` / reversed), a non-boolean control column, enforcement assertions (a rewritten CHECK must still REJECT a bad row — a constraint silently relaxed to a tautology would be worse than the bug), and the strftime DEFAULT round-trip incl. a defaulted INSERT. They were `t.Skip`-gated while the fix was pending; the skip is now REMOVED and all three pins run green. **Fix shipped:** an `inNode` (list form only — subquery, `IN <table>` and the PG-invalid empty list still refuse) plus a `sqEmitCtx` threaded through every emit so `SQLiteExprToPGBoolAware` can re-type 0/1 against boolean-promoted columns (`=`, `<>`/`!=`, reversed operands, and IN members; ORDERING comparisons and out-of-range literals like `flag = 2` deliberately NOT rewritten — PG rejects those loudly rather than sluice guessing). MySQL never rewrites: its BOOLEAN is TINYINT and takes 0/1 natively. The strftime set landed in `translateSQLiteDefaultExpr` (whole-format current-instant spellings only, second-precision preserved via `date_trunc(.second., now())` since PG.s bare `now()` carries microseconds; `%s` → `floor(extract(epoch from now()))`; partial formats and non-.now. bases still refuse). Severity: loud refusal / lossy default, never silent corruption — copied rows carry explicit values throughout.

**Target-side autovacuum / dead-tuple health during a migration or CDC catch-up — ✅ SHIPPED v0.99.288 (filed 2026-07-22 from the Hatchet "Postgres survival guide" review).** Most of that post is single-node OLTP operations and explicitly omits logical replication / WAL / slots, but one item lands squarely on sluice's workload: **autovacuum falling behind under sustained write volume**, with transaction-ID wraparound as the worst case. A sluice bulk copy into Postgres IS a sustained high-write workload, and so is a long CDC catch-up against a high-churn source — exactly the shape where dead tuples outrun vacuum. **Shipped as the ADR-0107 item-36 alerter's vacuum rule family**, following the item-45 sync-lag alerter's shape (probe-based, UNGATED from PlanetScale telemetry) rather than the snapshot rules: a new optional target-side probe `ir.TargetVacuumHealthReporter` (implemented by the Postgres `ChangeApplier` over the pool it already holds — `pg_stat_user_tables` worst-table dead-tuple ratio above a 1000-dead-tuple noise floor, plus `age(datfrozenxid)`), a sidecar started from `startTelemetrySidecars` so it covers cold-copy as well as CDC apply, the SAME `evalThresholdAlert` edge-trigger + cooldown + hysteresis decision and the same sinks. Two opt-in rules: `--notify-dead-tuple-ratio` (WARNING; body carries the worst table, dead/live counts, `last_autovacuum`, `autovacuum_count` — "running but losing" vs "never reached it" answered in the page) and `--notify-xid-age` (CRITICAL; wraparound headroom). Both on `sync start` + the fleet YAML. A configured rule against a non-Postgres target WARNs once and stays inert; a healthy zero-dead reading is a REAL observation that re-arms (distinct from probe-failure, which neither fires nor re-arms). Deliberately NOT added to the persisted `sluice_target_metrics_history` table (a stored codec — schema change out of scope for an advisory). Advisory/observability only, NOT a correctness gate: sluice's writes stay correct regardless; this is about telling the operator their target is accumulating bloat before it becomes a stall. Integration pin ground-truths the probe against real PG 16 (manufactured bloat + a sub-floor all-dead decoy that must not page). Other candidates from the post were already covered (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` + deferred index creation = ADR-0077/0080 index-build overlap; batching-for-throughput = ADR-0092's pipelined CDC apply, which measured ~48× vs their "~10×") or marginal (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on the ADR-0054 `LeaseManager` acquire path — one holder per table means contention is negligible, so not worth a change on current evidence). **EXPLICIT GAP — migrate mode (audit 2026-07-23 PERF-1, filed not implemented):** the vacuum advisories cover SYNC only (`startVacuumHealthNotifier` is a streamer sidecar off `startTelemetrySidecars`, so it reaches sync cold-copy + CDC apply); one-shot `migrate` — the docs' own named heaviest-write window — has no hook, because the `Migrator` has no notifier-sidecar seam (no `buildMetricsNotifier`, no notify flags on the migrate CLI surface). Wiring it means porting the sink/threshold flag set + a run-scoped sidecar onto `Migrator` — a deliberate S–M chunk, demand-gated (the long-lived sync is where the alerting pays; a migrate operator is typically watching the run). The MySQL-target sibling is separately deferred in `ir/target_vacuum_health.go` (InnoDB purge lag has a different signal shape). Declared in `docs/dev/perf-parity-matrix.md` row 26 per the perf-parity working agreement.

### Large-table exact count via OLAP workload mode ([ADR-0147](../adr/adr-0147-olap-large-table-counts.md)) — *IMPLEMENTED on main `4d3648de` (OLAP primary on vtgate flavors + WARN-logged chunked fallback); remaining follow-up = evaluate removing the chunked fallback once OLAP-count is field-proven*

**Why.** `verify`'s exact count fails on large PlanetScale tables. OLTP `count(*)` on a wide/clustered table (no cheap secondary index to auto-narrow to) is killed by PlanetScale's max-statement-execution-time limit — MySQL **errno 3024**, ~900 s — live-proven: a 49 GB PK-only table failed OLTP `count(*)` at ~661 s. Today `ExactRowCount` only survives this for single-integer-PK tables (via `chunkedCount`, which keeps each range query short); composite/string/UUID/no-PK tables fall to `singleShotCount` = plain `count(*)` and **fail at scale**.

**What.** Route the large-table count through OLAP: `SET workload='olap'` then `SELECT COUNT(*)` on a DEDICATED connection (never session-wide — the v0.99.15 lesson; mirror `row_reader.go`'s no-PK read). OLAP streams, so it is not bound by the OLTP statement-time limit — live-proven to complete the same 49 GB count in 1264 s, *identical* to chunked-PK (chunking is NOT faster; both are I/O-bound on the same clustered bytes). It works for every PK shape, closing the errno-3024 gap for the non-single-int-PK tables. Tables with a usable narrow secondary index keep plain `count(*)` (the optimizer auto-narrows → 4 s vs 244 s at 10 GB). Fix `singleShotCount`'s comment (the failure is statement-time errno-3024, not a "row-read limit").

**Gotchas / open questions.** (1) **Keep `chunkedCount` in place during the transition** — it works and is the same speed; make OLAP the primary, then a follow-up evaluates whether chunked can be fully removed (the operator's explicit "swap now, retire chunked later" sequencing — do not rip it out immediately). (2) The OLAP `SET` MUST be on a dedicated pooled connection returned clean — a leaked session-wide `workload=olap` is the v0.99.15 regression. (3) `estimate-first-then-exact` (information_schema cardinality pre-check) is an orthogonal fast-path lever, most valuable for exactly these large PK-only tables; not in scope here. (4) No Postgres change (payload TOASTs out-of-line → the count scan stays small).

### Deferred secondary-index creation exceeds PlanetScale's statement-time limit at scale — *RESOLVED for now: path (b) `--upfront-indexes` SHIPPED (`ef07c1da`) + errno-3024 → --upfront-indexes hint SHIPPED (hints.go); path (a) deploy-request SHIPPED v0.99.255 ([ADR-0148](../adr/adr-0148-planetscale-deploy-request-index-build.md), roadmap item 67)*

**Why.** sluice defers secondary-index creation to a post-copy phase that issues a plain `ALTER TABLE … ADD INDEX`. On a large PlanetScale-MySQL target that ALTER runs long enough to hit the max-statement-execution-time wall (**errno 3024**, ~900 s) — live-proven: `ADD INDEX` on a 49 GB table failed at ~901 s, leaving the data copied but the declared secondary index **not created** (recoverable only via `--resume`, which re-attempts the same failing ALTER). Large customers would hit this.

**What — two paths:**
- **(b) upfront-index mode — SHIPPED (`--upfront-indexes`, `ef07c1da`).** Runs the existing `CreateIndexes` phase BEFORE the bulk copy (in `runBulkCopyPhases`) so the INSERTs maintain the indexes; no post-copy ALTER, so the errno-3024 wall is never reached. Engine-neutral (reuses `CreateIndexes`), FKs stay deferred (indexes-only reorder → no ordering regression), opt-in (default deferred; zero-value-safe). **Benchmark (local MySQL, 3.2 M rows, 4 secondary indexes): deferred 29 s vs upfront 333 s → deferred ~11× faster** (post-copy `ADD INDEX` is a sort-based bulk build; upfront pays per-row B-tree maintenance). So upfront is a **reliability fallback, not a speed option**: on a PS target where deferred *fails*, the real choice is "fails vs 333 s that completes." Default stays deferred (fast); upfront is the escape hatch for PS-at-scale.
- **(a) PlanetScale deploy-request path — SHIPPED v0.99.255 ([ADR-0148](../adr/adr-0148-planetscale-deploy-request-index-build.md), roadmap item 67); the design context below is retained for history.** It was originally deferred because the toggle-lag finding kills the per-table auto-toggle, it needs extra credentials + the safe-migrations prerequisite, and the benchmark showed `--upfront-indexes` (~8–11× slower, but only on the opt-in case where deferred would fail anyway) plus the errno-3024 hint is good enough. Kept as the recorded validated design. *Correction:* `SET @@ddl_strategy='vitess'` does NOT work on PlanetScale — the direct `ALTER` runs *synchronously* and hits errno 3024 (proven). PS's async online DDL is driven by the **deploy-request workflow** (dev branch → `ALTER ADD INDEX` on it → deploy request into main → deploy via VReplication → poll → skip-revert → delete branch), which gets more time. **A live prototype (real PS-10, 2026-07-02) drove the whole chain via the PS API (thin HTTP client + service token, no `planetscale-go` SDK) and confirmed the index landed on main's data, intact.** **Design = AUTOMATIC FALLBACK:** because the deploy-request build is *post-copy on the already-migrated data* (like the direct `ALTER` it replaces), sluice can transparently swap to it when a deferred `ADD INDEX` hits errno 3024 — no re-copy, no operator action, no re-run. This **subsumes the "(B) error-guided" idea** (no need to tell the operator to re-run with `--upfront-indexes`). The true one-run auto-adjust: keeps the fast deferred load AND avoids the wall. Cost: the doomed direct `ALTER` burns ~900 s before the fallback engages (optional future `information_schema.DATA_LENGTH` probe could skip it for clearly-huge tables). Open design questions (ADR-0148): safe-migrations must be enabled on main (auto-enable vs require — and it blocks direct DDL thereafter); a PS API token + branch password are needed beyond the data-plane DSN; per-table vs whole-schema batching; failure/cleanup + revert finalization. Bigger PS-specific project; `--upfront-indexes` (b, shipped) remains the zero-dependency escape hatch.

**Gotchas / open questions.** The upfront path's cost is real (~11× on the benchmark); consider auto-selecting it only when the PS target is estimated large enough that deferred would fail (a size heuristic), rather than a blanket opt-in — open design question. Remaining test-program scenarios: the FK-deferred variant (upfront under FKs — PS forces it there) and larger upfront-vs-deferred sweeps. Same errno-class lineage as [ADR-0146](../adr/adr-0146-coldcopy-chunk-open-reconnect.md); the count-side sibling is [ADR-0147](../adr/adr-0147-olap-large-table-counts.md).

### 1. Vitess / vttestserver hardening track ([ADR-0073](../adr/adr-0073-vitess-internal-and-online-ddl-tables.md)) — *operator-flagged; (a)/(b1)/(b2)/(c)/(d)/(e) ALL SHIPPED (`422c522`/`30fe85b`/`7f742b8`). Track complete.*

**Why.** PlanetScale *is* Vitess, and it's sluice's make-or-break audience. **Online DDL is the default schema-change mechanism on Vitess**, so the `_vt_*` shadow / lifecycle tables it creates appear in essentially every real PlanetScale sync — and a *reproduced* gap (below) shows sluice's blanket `Match:"/.*/"` VStream filter pulls them in and can wedge the stream. This has to be rock-solid. Bug 126's fix (v0.99.6 — `vstream_*` DSN params no longer leak into the MySQL session) unblocks driving the CLI against `vttestserver`, which is what makes the test investment below possible.

**What.** A tiered effort:
- **(a) `vitess` self-hosted flavor — SHIPPED (`476b349`).** A sibling to the PlanetScale flavor (same VStream engine code, different defaults + `Capabilities`): sane self-hosted defaults (`vstream_transport=plaintext`, `vstream_auth=none`) so `--source-driver=vitess` "just works" without hand-set `vstream_*`. `FlavorVitess` is defined in `internal/engines/mysql/flavor.go`, registered in `engine.go:581`, gates every VStream-vs-binlog branch on `Flavor.usesVStream()` (so it is correct everywhere by construction), and aliases PlanetScale's `Capabilities` verbatim (`flavor.go:81` — diverge only on evidence; when a real capability difference surfaces, give `vitess` its own map entry and drop the alias). The self-hosted connection defaults are applied at `cdc_vstream.go:250` / `cdc_vstream_snapshot.go:123`. **Exercised end-to-end against the local self-hosted Vitess cluster** by the geometry/Bug-27 cluster test (below) — the cluster IS self-hosted Vitess, so it is the natural `FlavorVitess` target (the other cluster tests use `FlavorPlanetScale`).
- **(b1) vttestserver harness — DONE.** The integration harness now sets `ENABLE_ONLINE_DDL` (+ `NUM_SHARDS`); the internal-table exclusion is pinned here under `Integration (vstream)`. But vttestserver's vtcombo **cannot complete an online-DDL cutover** (the scheduler is stubbed), so it covers exclusion + the COPY/CDC paths, not the full rename-swap.
- **(b2) full Vitess compose-cluster harness — BUILT.** `startVitessCluster(t)` (`internal/engines/mysql/cdc_vstream_cluster_integration_test.go`, build tag `integration && vitesscluster`): a minimal custom `docker compose` (`testdata/vitesscluster/docker-compose.yml`) — etcd + vtctld + PRIMARY vttablet + REPLICA vttablet + vtgate, all on `vitess/lite:v24.0.1` (Vitess 24, in lockstep with the vendored `vitess.io/vitess v0.24.1` client) — that runs the **real** online-DDL scheduler, so it performs the VReplication copy + atomic rename cutover vtcombo can't (proven: a `ddl_strategy='vitess'` ALTER reaches `migration_status=complete`). Boot ~28 s, ~500 MB RSS. A separate, gated/manual job (not per-PR); the durable vehicle for cutover-survival **and** future resharding / FK-mode / multi-keyspace tests.
- **(c) online-DDL / `_vt_*` table-lifecycle robustness (CORRECTNESS-GATING) — SHIPPED + VALIDATED.** **Exclusion shipped v0.99.7** (`e9d5544`) — Vitess-internal tables dropped from COPY + CDC via `schema.IsInternalOperationTableName()` (version-dependent naming, [vitessio/vitess#14582](https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/issues/14582): legacy `_vt_HOLD/PURGE/EVAC/DROP` in 19–20 → unified `_vt_<op>_<uuid>_<timestamp>_`, op codes `hld/prg/evc/drp/vrp/gho/ghc/del`, in 20+), anchored to the helper not a static list. **Full cutover-survival VALIDATED on tier-2 (b2):** `TestVitessCluster_OnlineDDL_CutoverSurvivesWithZeroLoss` (300-row logical table, cold-start sync, real online ALTER mid-stream → `complete`, keeps writing through the new schema; asserts not-wedged + zero loss + post-cutover schema flows + no `_vt_*` row/refusal) and `TestVitessCluster_OnlineDDL_ComplexShapesSurviveCutover` (mid-table column DROP, ENUM ADD, ENUM value-set EXTEND) — **both PASS**. A robustness finding surfaced by (b2) — a **primary-only CDC-tail silent wedge** (hardcoded `TabletType_REPLICA` hung silently on a primary-only cluster, a loud-failure-tenet violation) — was **fixed** (`vstream_tablet_type` DSN knob + a liveness watchdog that fails loud) and pinned. See [ADR-0073](../adr/adr-0073-vitess-internal-and-online-ddl-tables.md).
- **(d) chaos harness on (b2) — resilience under real infra failures — DONE.** The `integration && vitesscluster && chaos` suite injects **primary failover (PRS + ERS)**, **vttablet/mysqld kill mid-cold-start**, **vtgate restart**, and **rolling Vitess upgrade** (v24.0.0 → v24.0.1) — each asserting: after the fault + recovery, target `COUNT == source` (zero loss/dup) **OR** sluice fails LOUDLY; never a silent partial/hang. **Full-suite green — all 4 scenarios** (`942b634`); tablet-kill proved **zero-loss across an EmergencyReparentShard**. A cross-engine-target chaos test (Vitess source restart mid-COPY → PG via Migrator) landed in v0.99.13 (`2f5f30f`). Gated/manual (heavy); a scheduled CI job is a possible follow-on.
- **(e) multi-Vitess-version matrix + end-to-end Bug 27 (VStream POINT) verification — SHIPPED (`422c522`/`7f742b8`).** Both pieces landed on the (b2) cluster, plus CI automation: the version-matrix scripts (`scripts/vitess-version-matrix.{ps1,sh}`, `scripts/vitess-versions.txt` single-source-of-truth), the Bug-27 e2e test (`cdc_vstream_cluster_geometry_integration_test.go`), the GHCR prebake mirror, and the scheduled `.github/workflows/vitess-version-matrix.yml` (Sun 08:00 + dispatch; not a required check). Two pieces of regression breadth on the (b2) cluster:
  - **Bug 27 end-to-end.** The SRID-prefix strip (`cdc_vstream.go:1354`, `decodeVStreamCell` Type_GEOMETRY) is unit-pinned and closed since v0.28.0, but the *operator-run* end-to-end leg was historically deferred to `psverify` (real PlanetScale, credentials-gated). The local self-hosted cluster is a sufficient and cheaper end-to-end target: a `vitesscluster`-tagged test seeds a `POINT` column, streams it via **`FlavorVitess`**, and asserts the decoded `ir.Geometry` value is valid WKB with the 4-byte SRID prefix stripped (ground-truthed against MySQL `ST_AsWKB`). Closes Bug 27's end-to-end column *and* gives `FlavorVitess` its first real-cluster exercise — no PlanetScale credentials required.
  - **Multi-version matrix (v21 → latest).** The compose file already takes `${VITESS_LITE_IMAGE}` and the harness inherits `os.Environ()`, so a version override flows through today. The added breadth: a version-looping runner (`scripts/vitess-version-matrix.{ps1,sh}`) sweeping `v21.0.x`, `v22.0.x`, `v23.0.x`, `v24.0.x` (lockstep with the vendored `vitess.io/vitess v0.24.1` client) plus a `latest` canary (allowed to skip/fail), the harness logging which image it booted, and an empirically-confirmed **support floor** recorded here. The vendored client stays v24.0.1; older servers are exercised via newer-client→older-server skew — the direction Vitess supports for rolling upgrades and the one PlanetScale itself runs. **Manual/rig-driven** (no recurring CI cost — matches the gated cluster suite); a scheduled cron matrix is a possible follow-on once the floor is confirmed. **First sweep (2026-06-08, `-Run TestVitessCluster_Bug27`):** `latest` / v24.0.1 / **v23.0.4 all PASS** (the v24 client streams VStream + Bug-27 SRID-strip correctly against a v23 server — newer-client→older-server skew confirmed one major back, and forward-compat against the newest server holds); **v21.0.6 / v22.0.4 FAIL** to boot — their *server* binaries (vtctld/vttablet/vtgate/mysqlctl) only accept the legacy **underscore** flag form (`--topo_implementation`, `--service_map`, …), while the base compose uses the modern hyphen form (canonical from v23). So the current empirical floor is **v23**. **Floor extended to v21 (DONE):** `docker-compose.legacy-flags.yml` carries the underscore-converted server commands (`vtctld`/`vttablet`/`vtgate` + the `mysqlctl` prelude); `vtctldclient` already uses hyphen on v21 so the topo-init calls are untouched, and `--tablet-path` / `--config-file-not-found-handling` correctly stay hyphen even on v21. `startVitessCluster` parses the major from `VITESS_LITE_IMAGE` (`vitessClusterMajor()`) and layers the override into every `docker compose` invocation **only when major ≤ 22** — v23/v24/latest stay on the clean hyphen form. **Full matrix now PASSES Bug 27 on v21.0.6 / v22.0.4 / v23.0.4 / v24.0.1 + `latest`** (v21/v22 with the override layered; v23/v24/latest without). **Empirical support floor = v21**, the requested range.

**Gotchas.** The reproduced bug (now fixed): during the Bug-125 hunt, sluice's COPY filter grabbed a `_vt_vrp_*` shadow during an in-flight deploy and tripped the ADR-0071 scope-mismatch refusal (zero rows) — so the exclusion covers BOTH the COPY filter and CDC dispatch. Anchor the matcher to Vitess's helper (not a static prefix list) + pin the recognized set AND a non-internal-lookalike battery (a false positive = a user table silently dropped from the migration). (c) was silent-loss-tier — "the first real schema change on PlanetScale breaks the sync" if wrong. **Sequence (all shipped): Bug 126 (v0.99.6) → (b1) vttestserver harness + (c) exclusion (v0.99.7) → (b2) compose harness BUILT → (c) full-cutover validation on (b2) PASS + primary-only wedge fixed (v0.99.7 arc) → (d) chaos suite green → (a) `vitess` flavor (`476b349`) → (e) multi-version matrix + Bug 27 end-to-end + scheduled CI matrix workflow (`422c522`/`7f742b8`).** The tier-2 cluster + chaos suites stay gated/manual (not per-PR CI); the scheduled version-matrix CI job shipped, so the track is complete.

**Follow-ups from the v0.99.7–v0.99.9 real-PlanetScale validation arc** (3 releases, 4 bugs found+fixed — Bug 127/128 → v0.99.8, Bug 129 → v0.99.9; logged, none blocking):
- **F1.** PS *production-branch* targets need an `admin`-role password (`readwriter` is denied control-table DDL) — operator-docs note.
- **F2.** `--force-cold-start` only skips the cold-start preflight; with a persisted position it still warm-resumes (the switch keys on `found`, not the flag). **Decided (2026-06-06): add a separate flag** (`--restart-from-scratch` / `--reset-position`) for the force-fresh-COPY intent; leave `--force-cold-start` as preflight-skip.
- **F3.** The v0.99.7 liveness watchdog disarms on the first snapshot VGTID, so a "tablet-serving-but-no-COPY-progress" stall hangs silently (loud-failure-tenet gap). Needs a **COPY-progress watchdog** (VGTID seen but no COPY row / `COPY_COMPLETED` within a window → fail loud). **Window must tolerate a legitimate slow COPY start:** a restored-from-backup PS production branch took **~2.5 min** before its first COPY row (vreplication/schema-engine warmup) then copied normally — so the v0.99.8-era "branch-side stall" on `main-restored-from-backup-2026-01-12` was a *slow start*, not a permanent stall (PK cold-start re-validated 2026-06-06). Best proven via the (d) chaos harness.
- **F4.** `TestADR0046_CrashInjectionMatrix_PG` is flaky ("branching/mis-stitched lineage", 3× in the v0.99.8/v0.99.9 CI; `gh run rerun --failed` clears it) — stabilization pass on the crash-injection manifest-lineage stitching, unrelated to the VStream work.

### 1b. Resilient, resumable VStream cold-start COPY ([ADR-0072](../adr/adr-0072-resumable-coldstart-copy.md)) — *SHIPPED v0.99.4–v0.99.5*

**Why.** A large-table PlanetScale cold-start that hits a transient network fault mid-COPY (`Unavailable: connector reset by peer`) currently has to restart the **entire** copy from row 0 — and for a multi-GB table over a flaky link, the re-copy may fault again before finishing, never converging. Steady-state CDC tailing already resumes from the last GTID and PG→PG copy-pool has AIMD backoff; the VStream cold-start COPY phase is the one long-running path with no resume.

**What.** Three interlocking gaps (full trace in ADR-0072):
- **Gap 1 — gRPC transient classification (SHIPPED).** `classifyReaderError` now honors native gRPC status codes (`Unavailable`/`Aborted`/`Unknown`/`ResourceExhausted` → retriable) instead of only MySQL-`1105`/raw-text shapes, so a VStream `Recv` reset triggers `runWithRetry` instead of failing terminally. `reader_errors.go` + `TestClassifyReaderError_GRPCStatusCodes`.
- **Gap 1.5 — idempotency prerequisite.** `runWithRetry` clears `ResetTargetData` after the first attempt (`streamer.go:884`), so a retry re-copies into a target holding the partial rows → non-retriable `1062` unless the COPY writer is idempotent. **Ties to the Bug 125 idempotent-COPY-writer fix; the two must ship together** or cold-start retry is inert.
- **Gap 2 — resumable COPY cursor (the design).** `shardGtid` drops Vitess's per-table `TablePKs` (the COPY-resume cursor); the position is persisted only at `COPY_COMPLETED`. Carry `TablePKs` in the position (Phase A), checkpoint it on a bounded cadence during COPY (Phase B), and reconnect-and-resume in the snapshot pump (Phase C).

**Gotchas.** Position format gains an additive field — pin that old tokens still decode to "COPY from beginning". Checkpoint cadence trades fault-loss-window vs. control-table write amplification (bounded N-rows/T-seconds, not per-row). Concurrency-adjacent (pump goroutine + in-place reconnect) → **`-race`-before-tag**. Validate jointly with the Bug 125 idempotency fix and ground-truth the resume row-count on a real Vitess target.

### 2. Apache Arrow integration (deferred — research-doc updated)

**Why.** Original conditional-yes recommendation in `design/apache-arrow-integration.md` was gated on logical-backup picking Parquet. **Phase 1 logical backups shipped JSON-Lines + gzip instead** (`internal/pipeline/backup_chunk.go:8-32`); the gate dissolved. Updated research lives in [`docs/research/apache-arrow-findings.md`](../research/apache-arrow-findings.md): Shape A (Arrow as IR row representation) is recommended **defer** — sizable refactor, zero current operator demand. The narrower analytics-export angle moved to its own research item — see item 9 below.

**What.** No code chunk. Revisit when an operator with a real Parquet/columnar requirement surfaces, or when item 8's research doc names a winning surface.

**Gotchas (preserved for the eventual revisit).** Silent type drift at Decimal-256 / Time-out-of-range / UUID-string-parse / Arrow-null-vs-empty-string boundaries — each needs explicit loud-failure branches per the loud-failure tenet. ~2× binary growth under the build tag (mitigated by keeping default untagged build slim). Shape C (Arrow as in-flight row-pipeline format) explicitly rejected as IR-tenet-violating.

---

### 3. Cross-table copy concurrency for many-table schemas (the pgcopydb many-table gap) — *(a) cross-table pool SHIPPED (ADR-0076); (b) adaptive threshold SHIPPED*

**Why.** A controlled PG → PG benchmark vs pgcopydb (the tool sluice's bulk-copy was modeled on; secondary session, 2026-06-07, written up in `docs/comparison-pgcopydb.md`) surfaced a real out-of-box gap on **many-table** schemas: `sluice migrate` has **no cross-table concurrency**. The per-table loop in `internal/pipeline/migrate.go` copies tables **serially**, and `--bulk-parallelism` only splits *within* a table (ADR-0019 PK-range chunking). pgcopydb's `--table-jobs` (default 4) copies multiple tables at once. On 30 tables × 50k rows (each below the 80k within-table-split threshold, so each is both single-streamed *and* serial), sluice's default was **16.1 s vs pgcopydb's 6.1 s (~2.6× slower)** — cores sit idle between tables. On a single large table sluice's default auto-split actually *wins* (5.05 s vs 6.14 s); the gap is specifically the many-medium-table shape. Correctness was never in question — every run was zero-loss (aggregate-checksum verified). This is a throughput/UX gap, not a silent-loss class, so it is demand/competitive-gated, not correctness-gating.

**What.** Two candidate directions (the benchmark draft names both; pick after a design pass):
- **(a) Cross-table copy concurrency — SHIPPED (ADR-0076).** A bounded `errgroup` worker pool over the per-table copy loop (`--table-parallelism`, default `0`=auto→4 à la pgcopydb's `--table-jobs`; `1` disables), composed *with* the existing within-table `--bulk-parallelism`. The two axes' connection budget is split at the SINGLE existing chokepoint (`resolveCopyParallelismBudget`): within is satisfied first, the table axis gets `budget/withinP`, so the product `tableP × withinP <= CopyBudget` holds **by construction** — no global shared gate (the rejected option ii). `--max-target-connections` bounds the product. Resume-under-concurrency extends the chunk axis's clone-under-lock discipline to every table-level state write (peer tables write distinct keys of the same map). The `migrate` path only; the sync cold-start path stays serial by design. Measured ~2.76× speedup (5.88s→2.13s) on the 30×50k benchmark shape, closing the ~2.6× pgcopydb gap; every run zero-loss. Pinned by unit tests (`resolveCopyParallelismBudget` product-bound matrix incl. budget=1 and `--max-target-connections`; table-pool peak-concurrency + all-complete) + 3 PG integration tests (many-table speedup, resume-under-concurrency mid-run kill, combined-budget on a small `max_connections` target).
- **(b) Adaptive `--bulk-parallel-min-rows` — SHIPPED.** `--bulk-parallel-min-rows` is now a `0 = auto` sentinel (was a fixed `80000` CLI default): an explicit value is honoured verbatim, but the auto path scales the within-table-split threshold DOWN as the table count rises (`default/tableCount`, floored at `10000`; `internal/pipeline/chunk.go` `resolveBulkParallelMinRows`). A single/few-table schema keeps the full default (the single-large-table auto-split win is unchanged); a many-medium-table schema now engages within-table parallelism instead of copying each medium table serially + single-streamed. Closes most of the gap with no new concurrency surface (tables still copied serially, so ≤ one table's connections open at once → no budget-math change). The benchmark measured 6.97 s vs pgcopydb 6.1 s (~14 %) with the threshold lowered by hand; this makes that automatic. Pinned by `TestResolveBulkParallelMinRows` (explicit-honoured / monotonic / floored / single-table-unchanged). Leaves the residual serial-table scheduling overhead, which (a) removes.

**Gotchas.** (1) **Resumability + checkpoint state** — the per-table `table_progress` cursor and the parallel-chunk `Chunks` state must stay correct under cross-table concurrency (peer tables writing the state row concurrently; the chunk path already guards its slice with a mutex + `cloneStateForWrite`, extend that discipline to the table axis). (2) **Connection budget** — cross-table × within-table parallelism multiplies open connections; the ADR-0043 budget preflight + the 53300 AIMD backoff gate must govern the *combined* count, not each axis independently, or a wide schema exhausts the target's connection slots. (3) **Snapshot consistency** — ADR-0019 already notes `migrate` uses per-connection snapshots (no shared snapshot for the cold migrate); more concurrent readers widens that window — fine for a quiesced source, but document it (the `sync start` cold-start path pins all readers to one exported snapshot via `ir.SnapshotImporter` and is unaffected). (4) **`-race`-before-tag** — this is a concurrency chunk.

**Operator demand check.** Competitive-gated: the gap only bites a *many-table* cold migrate at default settings, and it's tunable today (lower `--bulk-parallel-min-rows`). Promote when a real operator hits a slow wide-schema migrate, or alongside publishing the pgcopydb comparison (so the doc can say "known, tracked, tunable today"). Pairs naturally with finishing the `docs/comparison-pgcopydb.md` review (the draft's stated owner-review task).

---

### 3b. PG→PG copy throughput: index-build overlap + identity passthrough — *(a) index-build overlap SHIPPED (ADR-0077); (b) identity passthrough SHIPPED (ADR-0078)*

**Why.** The 110 GB / 43-table at-scale comparison (`docs/comparison-pgcopydb.md`, "At scale" section) showed pgcopydb **~1.75× faster end-to-end** (895 s vs 1564 s) on a realistic mixed corpus — *after* item 3 closed the cross-table gap. The remaining difference is two **structural** things (NOT parallelism — the run is disk-bound at ~100–122 MB/s; tuning workers/splitting did nothing or hurt). Both are concrete, independently-shippable optimizations.

**What.** Two separate chunks (each likely an ADR + a `-race`/value-fidelity pass):

- **(a) Overlap index builds with the copy — the broad win (every engine pair) — SHIPPED ([ADR-0077](../adr/adr-0077-overlap-index-builds-with-bulk-copy.md)).** `migrate` no longer runs a full bulk-copy phase *then* a separate deferred index phase (a sequential ~457 s tail at 110 GB — 29% of total — that pgcopydb hides by building each table's indexes as its data lands). On a PG target it now builds each table's secondary indexes as soon as its copy completes, concurrently with the still-copying tables, via the optional `ir.IncrementalIndexBuilder` surface: the copy pool's per-table success callback (`onTableCopied`) forwards each table onto a buffered channel that a separate index pool drains, both under one errgroup (copy error cancels index pool and vice versa). **Gotchas handled:** (1) the combined connection budget is split ONCE at the single chokepoint — `splitCopyAndIndexBudget` reserves `clamp(0.25×CopyBudget,1,8)` for the index pool and hands the rest to the copy axes, with the invariant `indexBudget + copyBudget' <= CopyBudget` (the index pool sizes from the reserved slice, NOT a self-probe, since copy connections are now open simultaneously); (2) constraints/FKs + identity-sync stay AFTER the combined phase; (3) resumability — `ir.TableProgress.IndexesBuilt` (additive on the wire) drives "copied-not-indexed → re-feed to index pool / fully-indexed → skip", with `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` guarding a crash mid-build; (4) `-race`-before-tag (concurrency chunk extending ADR-0076's pool — the `-race` Integration gate is CI-only). PG-only (the index-build-parallelism machinery is PG-only); MySQL falls back to the pre-existing post-copy whole-schema `CreateIndexes`. Pinned by unit tests (`splitCopyAndIndexBudget` invariant matrix; overlap-orchestrator fed-once/channel-closed/error-cancellation) + PG integration tests (overlap-actually-happens via `min(indexBuildStart) < max(copyComplete)` observability seam; zero-loss + all indexes via pg_indexes; resume short-circuits already-indexed tables; combined budget on a small max_connections target; MySQL fallback).

- **(b) PG→PG identity passthrough — closes the per-stream rate gap — SHIPPED ([ADR-0078](../adr/adr-0078-pg-pg-identity-passthrough-raw-copy.md)).** The IR copy decodes every row into the typed IR and re-encodes via `pgx.CopyFrom` — the per-stream gap the at-scale comparison measured (99.5 vs 122.6 MB/s, ~23%). A same-engine fast lane now byte-pipes the raw COPY stream (`COPY (SELECT <readable cols> [WHERE pk range]) TO STDOUT` → `io.Pipe` → `COPY tbl (<non-generated cols>) FROM STDIN`) via pgx's raw `pgconn` `CopyTo`/`CopyFrom`, escaping `database/sql` through the same `Conn.Raw` path `writeViaCopy` uses; composes with the chunk machinery (per-chunk byte-pipe) and the whole-table single-stream path. Engine-neutral OPTIONAL surfaces (`ir.RawCopyExporter`/`RawCopyImporter`/`RawCopyVersionProber`/`RawCopyChunk`/`RawCopyFormat`); MySQL doesn't implement them so a MySQL pair never takes the lane. **The GATE (the correctness-critical surface, one auditable pure predicate `rawCopyGate`):** same-engine (`Source.Name()==Target.Name()`, never naming "postgres") + no `--redact` + no `--type-override`/`--expr-override` + no shard-injection + per-table `identityProjection` (excludes extension/verbatim/bit/geometry — OID/wire-format-sensitive — in v1); any transform present → IR fallback (a miss would silently bypass a transformation, a silent-loss class). The CRUX sub-invariant: exporter projects an explicit SELECT of the source-readable columns (generated EXCLUDED), never a bare `COPY tbl TO STDOUT`; importer's column list comes from the SAME helper so they line up by construction. Cold-start + `migrate`-only (slotted in the ADR-0043 fast-loader branch; resume + sync stay on the IR path). Format: `--raw-copy-format=text|binary|auto`, default text (cross-major safe, pgcopydb's default); binary opt-in on a matched-server-major probe of both endpoints (mismatch → text loudly). Pinned by unit tests (`rawCopyGate` negative matrix per transform + all-clear positive; `identityProjection` per type family; `negotiateRawCopyFormat` downgrade; PG statement-builder projection-exclusion) + PG integration tests (positive zero-loss text+binary with raw-lane-taken seam; chunked; generated-column-recomputed; resume-falls-back; one negative-fallback per transform asserting raw NOT taken AND transform applied). `-race` concurrency chunk (local `io.Pipe`+2 goroutines per chunk inside the existing pools) → the `-race` Integration gate is CI-only. **Value-fidelity follow-up (shipped):** both raw sessions pin `client_encoding=UTF8` (`rawCopyForceUTF8`) before the COPY — the byte-pipe encodes under the source session's `client_encoding` and decodes under the target's, so an asymmetric DSN (`LATIN1` one side only) would silently corrupt non-ASCII text; forcing UTF8 on both makes the stream self-consistent by construction (the one place the raw lane asserts session state rather than passing bytes untouched).

**Operator demand check.** Competitive-gated (the pgcopydb-comparison story), operator-chosen 2026-06-08 to do next. (a) is the higher-value/broader; (b) is the headline per-stream-gap closer for the PG→PG audience. Reproduce the benchmark via `benchmarks/pgcopydb/`. **At-scale result (110 GB, measured 2026-06-09, `docs/comparison-pgcopydb.md`):** combined (a)+(b) closed the gap to pgcopydb from 1.75× → 1.42× (1564→1269 s), all zero-loss. Honest split: disk-bound, so (a) overlap was −60 s (overlapped index builds contend for the saturated disk) and (b) passthrough was the bigger lever at −235 s. Both are automatic/capability-detected (no flag), migrate-cold-start-only.

---

### 3c. Extend index-build overlap to MySQL targets — *SHIPPED v0.99.30, [ADR-0080](../adr/adr-0080-mysql-index-build-overlap.md) (`988ca79`); combined-`ALTER` follow-up SHIPPED (`591da65`)*

Re-land note: the first land regressed (its own overlap test hit `Error 1089` building a SPATIAL index) and was reverted; root cause was a PRE-EXISTING emit bug — `emitIndexColumnList` rendered the column prefix `(N)` on SPATIAL/FULLTEXT indexes (the reader surfaces a SUB_PART on the geometry column), which MySQL rejects. Fixed by suppressing the prefix for those kinds (also fixes the serial `CreateIndexes` path). Re-landed via PR with the `-race` gate green BEFORE main.

**Measured (`benchmarks/mysql/`):** −13 % median total wall (−21 % best case), MySQL→MySQL 30×1.5 M, 4 indexes/table, 10.7 GiB, disk-bound — a clear repeatable win (the serial post-copy index tail ~1432–1500 s, *larger than the copy*, folds into the copy window). Unlike ADR-0077's PG −60 s regression. The bench surfaced the within-table MDL serialization (per-`ALTER` metadata lock serializes a table's N indexes), which motivated the **combined-`ALTER` follow-up** (`591da65`): build a table's combinable BTREE/UNIQUE indexes in one `ALTER … ADD INDEX a, ADD INDEX b` (one InnoDB scan, one MDL), FULLTEXT/SPATIAL each separate (Error 1795 / no-LOCK=NONE). **Measured incremental: −18.1 % median** (combined median 1783 s vs per-index overlap 2177 s; per-pair −15 %/−21 %; all zero-loss + all-indexes) — a further win on top of the −13 % overlap. See the ADR-0080 amendment.

**Why.** Index-build overlap (ADR-0077, item 3b(a)) is engine-NEUTRAL in concept but PG-only in implementation: it engages only when the target writer implements `ir.IncrementalIndexBuilder`, which today only the PG writer does. MySQL-target migrates therefore still run the pre-ADR-0077 order — full bulk-copy phase, *then* a separate whole-schema `CreateIndexes` tail. A MySQL target would get the same tail-collapse the PG target got, for free on every MySQL-*target* migrate (MySQL→MySQL and PG→MySQL).

**What.** Implement `ir.IncrementalIndexBuilder` (+ the `TableIndexedNotifier` / completion-channel surface ADR-0077 defined) on the MySQL `SchemaWriter`: build a table's secondary indexes via `ALTER TABLE … ADD INDEX` (or multiple in one ALTER) as soon as its copy lands, concurrently with the still-copying tables, under the same combined connection budget (`splitCopyAndIndexBudget`). Constraints/FKs stay a final phase. PKs are already created with the table. The orchestrator change is zero — it already routes to the overlapped phase whenever the surface is present; this is purely the engine-side implementation + its budget participation.

**Gotchas.** (1) MySQL/InnoDB online-DDL `ADD INDEX` has different cost/locking characteristics than PG's `CREATE INDEX` (inplace vs copy algorithm, metadata locks, the row-log) — measure at scale before claiming a win; the PG number doesn't transfer. (2) PlanetScale/Vitess targets route DDL through their own online-DDL/Safe-Migrations machinery, so the overlap may be a no-op or need to defer to the platform — gate on flavor. (3) Concurrent `ALTER`s against the same instance compete for `innodb_buffer_pool` + I/O exactly like the PG disk-contention finding — the at-scale win may again be modest on a saturated disk and larger on fast storage. (4) `-race` chunk (extends the cross-table pool). Its own at-scale `benchmarks/pgcopydb/`-style MySQL measurement before the doc claims a number.

### 3d. Fast cold-start for the `sync` path — the pgcopydb `--follow` equivalent at full speed — *v1 SHIPPED v0.99.29; v1.1 (within-table chunking) SHIPPED v0.99.30 (`509fdeb`), [ADR-0079](../adr/adr-0079-fast-cold-start-for-sync-path.md) + v1.1-CORRECTION addendum*

v1.1 re-land note: the first v1.1 land regressed broadly (relaxing pinned-reader `CountRows` let the during-copy ETA probe race the row-stream on the pinned conn → `bad connection` → 0 rows) and was reverted. Re-designed: `CountRows` stays returning 0 for pinned readers (ETA probe safe by construction); a new `ir.RowCountEstimator` serves the pre-stream chunk decision off a FRESH non-pinned conn. value-fidelity-reviewer SHIP; the exact regression tests + a within-table-chunking-engaged pin pass locally; re-landed via PR with `-race` green on the combined state BEFORE main.

**Why.** This is the migrate-vs-sync gap a user hit: today the three cold-start speedups — cross-table pool (`--table-parallelism`, ADR-0076), index-build overlap (ADR-0077), and PG→PG raw passthrough (ADR-0078) — are **`migrate`-only**. `sync start`'s own initial cold-start calls the serial `runBulkCopyWithOpts` (`streamer.go:2811`, `streamer_multidb.go:587`) "serial by design," so the **copy-then-continuously-follow** workflow (pgcopydb's `--follow`; sluice's `sync start` is the one-command equivalent) does the initial copy on the SLOW path. There is also no clean `migrate` (fast) → `sync start` (CDC, no re-copy) handoff: `sync start` re-runs its own cold-start. So a user who wants *both* a fast initial copy *and* continuous CDC currently can't get the fast copy. pgcopydb gives fast-copy + follow together; sluice should too.

**What — two candidate shapes (pick after a design pass):**
- **(A) Bring the fast machinery to the sync cold-start.** Route `sync start`'s cold-start through the same parallel-pool + overlap + (for same-engine no-transform) raw-passthrough path `migrate` uses. The reason it's "serial by design" is the resumable-checkpoint coupling (the durable mid-COPY cursor that lets an interrupted cold-start warm-resume, ADR-0072) — so the work is making the fast paths checkpoint-compatible (the cross-table pool already threads `state.TableProgress`; the raw byte-pipe is the hard one — it has no per-row checkpoint granularity, so it would degrade to IR on the resumable path and engage only on a fresh/`--restart-from-scratch` cold-start, exactly as the migrate resume path already does).
- **(B) A `migrate` → `sync` position handoff.** `migrate` takes a consistent snapshot; if it recorded that snapshot's CDC start position (binlog GTID / PG LSN at snapshot time) into a manifest, `sync start --position-from-manifest`-style could begin CDC from there WITHOUT re-copying — reusing the existing chain-terminal handoff plumbing (`--position-from-manifest` already does this for backup chains). This keeps `migrate` and `sync` as separate fast primitives and bridges them, rather than fattening the sync cold-start.

**Gotchas.** (A) is the better UX (one command, like pgcopydb `--follow`) but couples the fast paths to the checkpoint machinery; (B) is lower-risk (reuses backup-chain handoff) but is a two-command workflow and needs `migrate` to capture+persist the consistent CDC start position (it takes the snapshot but may not persist a resumable CDC position today — verify). Either way: the snapshot/CDC boundary must stay gap-free (the FTWRL / exported-snapshot boundary discipline from the v0.99.16 silent-loss fix applies). `-race` chunk. Design-pass (Plan agent) before building; own ADR.

### 3e. Parallel writer fan-out on the VStream/CDC snapshot cold-start copy (the PS-MySQL throughput gap) — *SHIPPED v0.99.65 (ADR-0097; `ir.ParallelIdempotentCopyWriter`, `internal/pipeline/copy_fanout.go`)*

**Why.** Item 3d brought the FAST parallel cold-start to the `sync` path, but only for sources whose snapshot can be PK-range-chunked on the READ side (exported-snapshot PG, raw passthrough). The **VStream/PlanetScale-MySQL** cold-start cannot: vtgate streams the snapshot down one logical channel (no arbitrary range-`SELECT`), and PlanetScale blocks `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE`, so the writer falls back to a SINGLE cross-region-RTT-bound batched-`INSERT` connection (~13 GB/h). A live experiment proved N independent `sync` processes scaled near-linearly (N=3 → ~128 GB/h), beating PG single-stream COPY at N≥3–4.

**What.** The WRITE-side analogue of ADR-0019's read-side chunking: one reader goroutine PK-hash-partitions the single incoming snapshot row stream to N per-worker channels; N writer workers each run the existing idempotent batched-INSERT core on their own pinned connection. Engine-neutral pipeline routing + a new opt-in `ir.ParallelIdempotentCopyWriter` capability (MySQL implements; PG stays serial). See [ADR-0097](../adr/adr-0097-parallel-writer-fanout-vstream-snapshot-copy.md).

**Gotchas.** Exactly-once routing (no drop/dup; every row to one worker) is silent-loss-class. No position advances until every worker is durably flushed (ADR-0007 handoff). The ADR-0072 mid-COPY durable-progress checkpoint is DISABLED on fan-out tables (a flat flushed-row count is not order-equivalent to the enqueue frontier across workers → a mid-COPY breadcrumb could checkpoint past an un-flushed early row, silent-loss-on-resume); the whole-table join is the sole durability guarantee for a fanned-out table. PK-hash (not round-robin) so Bug-125 COPY re-emissions of a PK serialize on one worker. Zero-value-safe degree int (`0`→default; the v0.99.51 trap). Resume composes via the ADR-0098 auto-shard-aware resume (the fan-out runs against the one active table at a time, fresh or resumed). `-race` chunk — the integration `-race` gate is the merge gate and MUST be green before any tag.

---

### 3f. Auto-shard-aware VStream cold-copy resume (bounded-memory resume of a large multi-table keyspace) — *SHIPPED v0.99.67 (ADR-0098; `resolveResumeAutoShard`/`reopenForTableSeeded`, `cdc_vstream_copy_concurrency_pump.go`)*

**Why.** ADR-0095 (item 3, v0.99.62) made the VStream cold-copy auto-shard by table (one single-table COPY at a time, bounded memory) — but only on a FRESH cold-start (`start == nil`). A `--resume` (`OpenSnapshotStreamFromPosition`, a position carrying the ADR-0072 `TablePKs` cursor) fell back to the LEGACY single keyspace-wide interleaved stream → ADR-0071 buffer-cap **crash-loop**. Found live (BUG-CATALOG Bug 156): a resumed 28-table / 302 GB keyspace copy crash-looped (`table "binary_blobs" would buffer … exceeding --max-buffer-bytes … while "audit_trail" is being copied`); loud but FATAL-for-resume — the interleaved path can never make progress on a large keyspace, so resume of exactly the case auto-shard exists for was broken. ADR-0095 called this "a v1 limitation, not a correctness gap" — the live finding proves it is not benign.

**What.** Drop the `start == nil` gate (`autoShard := len(tables) > 1 && !singleStream`); drive the SAME per-table pump on resume. The persisted cursor names exactly the one in-progress table (`resolveResumeAutoShard`); re-copy the tables before it idempotently (Bug-125 upsert absorbs the overlap), resume that table from its cursor (`reopenForTableSeeded`, no row-0 restart), copy the tables after it fresh, and reuse the ADR-0095 per-shard GTID-set-min stitch for the CDC handoff. See [ADR-0098](../adr/adr-0098-auto-shard-aware-vstream-resume.md).

**Gotchas.** Gapless exactly-once across the resume seam is silent-loss-class: every in-scope table must contribute a captured per-table snapshot so the set-min stitch is the cold-start stitch (re-copy the finished prefix rather than skip it — skipping needs a persisted GTID floor + interval-min arithmetic over GTID sets, the Bug-74 risk class). CDC is recorded only at the LAST table's completion → never advances past an incompletely-copied table (ADR-0007). Bounded memory because exactly one single-table COPY is ever in flight. State-shape: NO new token field (completion re-derived from the cursor + table order). Back-compat: a released-code single-in-progress-table cursor round-trips; a legacy multi-table / out-of-scope cursor is REFUSED loudly (never silent re-copy/skip). `-race` chunk — the integration `-race` gate is the merge gate and MUST be green before any tag.

### 5. Translator catalog continuation

**Status (v0.38.0).** Twenty-eight of 30 catalog rules shipped after a second re-assessment pass. v0.35.0 landed 6 rules; v0.37.0 added 3 more (TIMESTAMPDIFF, JSON_OBJECT/ARRAY, LAST_DAY); v0.38.0 added 3 more from rule #10's hash family (MD5 unconditional via PG core; SHA1 + SHA2 gated on `--enable-pg-extension pgcrypto`). pgcrypto joins the extension catalog as a presence-gate (no types) — sluice's preflight confirms it's installed on the target before the SHA rewrites fire. The remaining 5 rules stay deferred per the catalog's load-bearing per-rule analysis:

- **#11 GREATEST/LEAST** — same function name in both engines but NULL semantics differ; auto-rewrite would mask divergence.
- **#13 REGEXP_LIKE** — MySQL ICU vs PG POSIX regex flavours diverge beyond clean rewrite.
- **#21 FIND_IN_SET** — full position semantic needs a LATERAL subquery, invalid in CHECK/GENERATED contexts.
- **#23 CONVERT_TZ** — AT TIME ZONE has subtle timestamp-vs-timestamptz semantics.
- **#29 INET_ATON/INET_NTOA** — no portable PG equivalent without a custom function.

All five have an actionable workaround via `--expr-override`. The remaining gaps would only land if a real operator workflow surfaces one of the deferred shapes as a regression — at which point the catalog's per-rule analysis already names the cost.

### 9. Multi-source aggregation — MySQL native parity

**Why.** v0.25.0's `--target-schema` is PG-only by design (PG schemas are first-class; MySQL collapses schema-and-database). MySQL operators with the same multi-source-microservices pattern get equivalent coverage today via `--target` DSN choice (different MySQL databases on the same server). For most operators this is enough — the analytics queries cross databases the same way they would cross PG schemas, and MySQL's namespace model genuinely is "database = schema."

**What.** If a real operator surfaces "I want N sluice processes targeting one MySQL server but landing in one logical database with namespacing," the design would need to invent a per-table prefix mechanism (option (b) from the proto-ADR's schema-collision discussion: `table_renames: { source_table: target_table }` mapping). New CLI flag `--rename-table SOURCE=TARGET` mirrored on each source's stream.

**Gotchas.** Per-table renaming is more verbose than schema-prefixing, but the proto-ADR notes it's the universal flexible option. Hardest UX problem: keeping the rename map in sync with source-side schema changes (operator must update the map when a source adds a table).

**Operator demand check.** Currently zero. The DSN-choice workaround is good enough for the cases sluice has seen. Track here so the option doesn't get lost; revisit when an operator asks.

### 10. PlanetScale MySQL+Vitess test-matrix expansion

**Why.** Default Vitess/VStream coverage runs against container-based Vitess (vttestserver, via the `integration vstream` build tag) in the normal test flow. Sluice also has a `psverify` build-tag harness for source coverage against a real PlanetScale endpoint (requires PlanetScale credentials), which is operator-run on-demand before releases rather than continuously exercised in CI. Several VStream-specific edge cases live in this gap:

- **Bug 27** (VStream POINT bytes mis-parsed) is the canonical example — explicitly deferred to the "GEOMETRY/SPATIAL support" entry's Phase B because the test infrastructure is operator-run.
- **Mid-stream MySQL Phase 2.5** — VStream is a separate code path from vanilla MySQL binlog. v0.27.0's MySQL Phase 2 (ADR-0034 filter-flip mechanism) ships only the binlog-source path. VStream's own table-scope semantics (per-shard streams, COPY-mode handoff) need their own analysis before the same `--no-drain` UX can extend to PlanetScale operators. Demand-driven; track here when an operator surfaces a real PS workload that needs live add-table.
- **PlanetScale Postgres slot lifecycle** — Patroni-managed; slot loss on failover is silent without `Logical slot name` cluster config (operator memory `project_planetscale_postgres_slots.md`). The check is documented in `docs/postgres-source-prep.md` but not exercised in CI.
- **VStream POINT/POLYGON/cross-shard-PK edge cases** — generally any PS-specific behavior beyond what vanilla MySQL exhibits.

**What.** Three paths (Path C added 2026-05-10 alongside the Vultr-box bootstrap):

- **Path A — Operator-run coverage matrix.** Document a "before each release" PlanetScale checklist: spin up a PS branch, run sluice against it for the canonical scenarios (vanilla migrate, CDC stream, slot recovery, geometry types, slot rename via `--slot-name=Logical slot name`). Output: `docs/dev/notes/ps-release-checklist.md`. ~1 day to write + populate; no code chunk.
- **Path B — CI-integrated coverage.** Move `psverify` (and/or `vstream`) from operator-run to CI-conditional (PR labels, scheduled workflows). Requires a non-revocable PlanetScale credential surface in CI; operationally heavier. Defer until Path C's signal surfaces enough recurring gaps to justify the CI cost.
- **Path C — pre-release validation pass.** Runs `integration vstream` (vttestserver-based VStream coverage) on every release-validation pass without burning CI minutes, via a provision-on-demand validation VM. Reference timing: ~4 min per run. Captures the Vitess-side coverage gap CI explicitly skips for cost. The remaining gap vs `psverify` is real-PlanetScale-specific behavior (TLS, vendor pgwire-proxy quirks); Path A still covers that surface.

**Operator demand check.** Path C closed the loop on the most-frequent vstream-edge-case worry without a CI cost spike. Path A remains the right answer for PlanetScale-specific quirks. Path B is a "if PS coverage gaps keep biting *and* Path C alone isn't enough" follow-on.

### 11. PG → PG extension passthrough — Tier 3 (uuid-ossp + pgcrypto function-defaults) — *SHIPPED v0.65.0 (`837769c`, ADR-0044)*

**Status:** the entire ADR-0032 v1 shortlist **SHIPPED** — framework + pgvector (v0.26.0), pg_trgm (v0.30.0), hstore + citext (v0.31.0, with the hstore PG→PG binary COPY codec landing in v0.32.1 / Bug 48 in v0.31.1), PostGIS (v0.33.0, with Bugs 49–53 closing geography / SP-GiST / BRIN / Z-M-ZM dimensional follow-ups through v0.33.3). pgcrypto joined the catalog as a presence-gate (no types) in v0.38.0 for the SHA1/SHA2 translator rules. See "Recently landed: PG → PG extension passthrough — v1 shortlist complete" + [ADR-0032](adr/adr-0032-pg-extension-passthrough.md) (status block records all five under "shipped").

**Why (Tier 3 — shipped).** uuid-ossp + pgcrypto are universal across all four hosted-PG providers, but their hard part is the **function-default catalog** (`uuid_generate_v4()`, `gen_random_uuid()`, pgcrypto `digest()` / `crypt()` in column DEFAULT / GENERATED bodies), not the type passthrough. The type-passthrough machinery is done; Tier 3 is an expression-translator-catalog chunk, not a new IR/engine surface.

**What.** Per-extension expression-translator catalog entries so a PG → PG passthrough preserves `DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4()` / pgcrypto function-defaults verbatim, with loud failure on cross-engine unless explicitly translated (parallel to ADR-0016's policy). pgcrypto's presence-gate already exists from v0.38.0; uuid-ossp would add the analogous catalog entry. **[ADR-0044](adr/adr-0044-extension-function-defaults-tier3.md) (Accepted 2026-05-16) SHIPPED in v0.65.0 (`837769c`).** The opt-in gate is live: extension-function defaults/generated-exprs require `--enable-pg-extension <ext>` and are refused early-and-clearly otherwise (a deliberate behaviour change vs. the prior implicit pass-through; core PG functions like `gen_random_uuid()` / `now()` are never gated). Code: `internal/engines/postgres/extension_function_gate_test.go` (the gate), `extension_catalog.go` (uuid-ossp `uuid_generate_v1/v4` + pgcrypto `digest`/`crypt` default gating), `expr_translate.go`. ADR-0032 §"Consequences" named this as the natural Tier 3 chunk; it is now closed.

**Gotchas.** Extension version skew (v1 checks presence, not version) is a documented limitation that carries forward. Cross-engine `DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` → MySQL is already handled (Bug 42, v0.23.1); Tier 3 is specifically the *PG → PG passthrough fidelity* of the function-default expressions plus uuid-ossp's `uuid_generate_*` family.

**Operator demand check.** Demand-gated — promote when a real operator surfaces a PG → PG sync where uuid-ossp / pgcrypto function-defaults round-trip incorrectly. Estimated ~150–300 LOC + ADR-0032 catalog-table update + integration tests.
