### 74. Vitess/VStream partial-row-image cell (filed from the Bug-193 review N4, 2026-07-17) — *✅ SHIPPED v0.99.272 ([ADR-0172](../adr/adr-0172-vstream-partial-row-image-belt.md); the belt at `dispatchRow`); the cold-start `dispatchCDCRow` mirror wiring gap (audit 2026-07-17 A1) closed v0.99.273*

The VStream reader (`cdc_vstream.go`, `decodeVStreamRow` ~:1588) passed row images through without a partial-image preflight or a `RowChange.DataColumns` bitmap check. A self-hosted Vitess deployment whose underlying mysqlds run `binlog_row_image=NOBLOB`/`MINIMAL` (Vitess 16+ supports it and then populates `DataColumns`) would hit the Bug-193 silent-loss class through the VStream door — unprobed and unguarded. PlanetScale manages FULL, so the managed flavor is safe; only self-hosted Vitess reaches it.

**Shipped as a decode-time bitmap belt, not a preflight** (VStream talks to a vtgate, not the tablets' mysqlds — there is no single `@@GLOBAL.binlog_row_image` to read; a self-hosted Vitess is a fleet of tablets, each with its own mysqld). `refuseVStreamPartialRowImage` (`cdc_vstream_partial_row_image.go`) runs per-RowChange in `dispatchRow` before decode: an UNSET bit in `RowChange.DataColumns` (a NOBLOB-omitted after-image column, which Vitess encodes as a NULL cell `decodeVStreamRow` would mis-read as a genuine NULL) refuses loudly with `SLUICE-E-CDC-ROW-IMAGE-PARTIAL` (reused — same silent-loss class as the vanilla binlog belt); a SET bit in `RowChange.JsonPartialValues` (a `binlog_row_value_options=PARTIAL_JSON` diff value) refuses too. Refuse, not carry-forward: NOBLOB omits the unchanged blob from the before image as well, so the event does not carry the prior value — reconstructing it would mean reading the target (replica-apply semantics sluice does not attempt). NOBLOB omits only UPDATE after-images (INSERT/DELETE log every column), so the after-image belt covers the whole class. Ground-truthed against vendored Vitess v0.24.2 (`RowChange.DataColumns` = "bit set if column present in after image", `Count` = full column count, bit order = vttablet `isBitSet` = little-endian within byte). Pinned by unit tests across the row-image-posture matrix (no-bitmap / full-bitmap / leading-/middle-/trailing-omitted / partial-JSON × INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), both direct on the belt and through the real `dispatch` path (partial UPDATE stops loudly and emits nothing). **CONCURRENCY chunk (VStream CDC path) — the `-race` Integration gate must pass on CI before any tag.** Recommended follow-up validation: a cluster-level pin with a self-hosted Vitess-24 mysqld set to `binlog_row_image=NOBLOB` + the `AllowNoBlobBinlogRowImage` experimental flag (the `vitesscluster` gated suite / `vitess-cluster-validator`), which the unit pins stand in for until run.

### 73. MariaDB flavor support (operator-requested 2026-07-16; SCOPED via live probe — full matrix + phased draft in the operator's sluice-testing `workspace/mariadb/scoping-probe.md`) — *✅ SHIPPED: P1 v0.99.268 ([ADR-0168](../adr/adr-0168-mariadb-flavor-phase1.md)), P2 v0.99.270 ([ADR-0169](../adr/adr-0169-mariadb-flavor-phase2.md)), P3 domain-GTID CDC v0.99.271 ([ADR-0170](../adr/adr-0170-mariadb-flavor-phase3-cdc.md)), P3 native uuid/inet CDC decode v0.99.272 ([ADR-0171](../adr/adr-0171-mariadb-native-uuid-inet-cdc-decode.md)). All phases live — see the per-phase sub-bullets below.*

**Why:** MariaDB is the largest MySQL-adjacent install base sluice doesn't serve. The 2026-07-16 scoping probe (mariadb:11.4 + 10.11, shipped v0.99.263 binary) found the gap smaller than feared: **no silent-loss path is reachable today** — every leg fails loudly, pre-data — and the vendored go-mysql v1.15.0 already carries complete MariaDB GTID support (`MariadbGTIDSet`, `StartSyncGTID`, probed working), so even CDC is plumbing rather than library work. `restore` INTO MariaDB 11.4 already works byte-identically (minus `POINT SRID` spelling).

**What (phased per the probe's draft):**
- **P1 (M) — SHIPPED (ADR-0168): bulk source+target via a `mariadb` flavor with honest capabilities; CDC refused loudly.** The source choke point is one I_S query (`schema_reader.go` `srs_id` + `statistics.expression` — MySQL-8-only columns, now flavor-gated to constants); the target choke is the 8.0.19+ row-alias upsert (`AS new ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`) in the migrate-state store + change applier + batched row writer + position/schema-history writes (MariaDB spelling: flavor-gated `VALUES()`, threaded through the whole class of emission sites). **ATOMIC with the query fix: the COLUMN_DEFAULT shim** (`translateMariaDBDefault`) — MariaDB reports quoted literals, the bare `NULL` keyword, `current_timestamp()` with empty `extra`, escape-encoded binary defaults; the shim classifies on surface form and produces byte-identical IR to a MySQL 8 read (unit parity matrix + live three-server integration matrix). Version floor: MariaDB **10.11 LTS**; the emitter remaps `utf8mb4_0900_*` ↔ `utf8mb4_uca1400_*` (present on both LTS lines) with a per-table/per-column WARN so default-collation schemas cross both directions. Connect-time server-fingerprint guard (mariadb-flavor-on-MySQL = coded refusal; mysql-flavor-on-MariaDB = steering WARN), SEQUENCE/SYSTEM VERSIONED census refusal, and coded `SLUICE-E-CDC-MARIADB-UNSUPPORTED` on every CDC surface via the new `ir.CDCUnsupportedExplainer`. CI: `mariadb:11.4` + `mariadb:10.11` integration legs. **NOTE: touches the schema reader + state store + change applier — the concurrency-adjacent state-store/applier changes must land through CI's `-race` Integration job before any tag (the Windows dev box is CGO=0).**
- **P2 (M) — SHIPPED (ADR-0169): MariaDB-specific type fidelity.** JSON identity: a `longtext` column whose ONLY CHECK is exactly `json_valid(<that column>)` remaps to `ir.JSON{Binary:false}` and that MariaDB-internal auto-CHECK is STRIPPED from the IR (so it no longer emits an invalid `json_valid()` CHECK on a PG target — the Phase-1 loud-failure is now a clean carry); a complex/other-column json_valid CHECK is precisely NOT mis-detected. Native `uuid`/`inet6`/`inet4` read to `ir.UUID{}`/`ir.Inet{}` (INET4 collapses to Inet); cross-engine emit is PG native / MySQL-family CHAR(36)/VARCHAR(45) (same-engine mariadb target lands CHAR(36)/VARCHAR(45) too — values lossless, native-type emit is a filed refinement). System-versioned tables and SEQUENCEs stay a LOUD census refusal upgraded to per-class remedies (carrying a versioned table as plain current-state silently drops temporal history; the IR Sequence surface is PG-only so half-mapping a MariaDB sequence would just relocate the failure to emit time — do NOT half-map). Geometry `ExtGeometry` now declared, round-trip closed BOTH ways: **SRID READ from `information_schema.GEOMETRY_COLUMNS.SRID` (NOT `REF_SYSTEM_ID` from SHOW CREATE — MariaDB does not echo it, ground-truth-corrected on 11.4/10.11), and WRITTEN as the `REF_SYSTEM_ID=<n>` TYPE attribute (before NOT NULL; MariaDB rejects MySQL 8's `SRID <n>`), the mariadb emitter carrying the target flavor.** Post-review fixes folded in: F1 (CRITICAL) — `migcore.IsMySQLFamilyEngine` had excluded `mariadb`, silently skipping every PG-native cross-engine refusal on PG→mariadb (dropped EXCLUDE constraints); fixed by delegating to the registry-parity-tested `translate.IsMySQLFamily` + a migcore registry-parity test; F2 (standalone sequence on the same path) resolved by F1; F3 the geometry emit above; Bug 198 (HIGH) — the check-constraint join fanned out on MariaDB (per-table constraint names), fixed with a flavor-gated `AND cc.table_name = tc.table_name` (MySQL-8 has no such column — left byte-identical). Pinned: unit family-matrices + live 11.4/10.11 reads (geometry SRID family × {0,4326}; JSON identity; check-fanout) + mariadb↔PG cross-engine round-trips (uuid/inet/json/NULL, PostGIS geometry value+SRID both directions) + PG→mariadb loud-refusal migrate pins.
- **P3 (L) — SHIPPED (ADR-0170): CDC with domain GTIDs.** The flavor declares `ir.CDCBinlog`; the binlog reader flavor-branches every format-sensitive surface off `FlavorMariaDB` (MySQL-8 path byte-identical). GROUND-TRUTH-CORRECTED against live 11.4 + 10.11 during implementation — **two of the roadmap draft's premises were false and are documented in ADR-0170:** (1) the "per-tx dummy QueryEvent → blanket schema-cache invalidation" perf trap **does not exist** — MariaDB emits NO BEGIN/dummy QueryEvent for plain DML (the domain-GTID event opens the transaction; a plain-DML tx is `MARIADB_GTID → TABLE_MAP → ROWS → XID`), so NO filter was added (adding an over-broad one would have risked the silent-DDL-drop the task guards); pinned that N plain-DML transactions invalidate the cache ZERO times while a real ALTER invalidates once. (2) `SHOW BINLOG STATUS` is accepted on 10.11 AND 11.4 already (not just 12); `SHOW MASTER STATUS` also works on both, and `SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS` (MySQL 8.4) fails 1064 — the fallback list is now `{SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS, SHOW MASTER STATUS, SHOW BINLOG STATUS}` (forward-compat for 12, zero extra round-trip on any current server). Load-bearing correctness: the pump handles `*replication.MariadbGTIDEvent` (which the vanilla pump ignored) to accumulate the domain GTID (else every emitted position stalls at cold-start = silent wrong-resume) and to emit `TxBegin` (MariaDB has no BEGIN QueryEvent). Cold-start position = `@@gtid_binlog_pos` (binlog GTID, NOT `@@gtid_current_pos` which folds in the slave position); GTID auto-detect returns true unconditionally (MariaDB has no `gtid_mode` variable). **Reachability (highest-risk silent-gap):** MariaDB has NO SQL pre-check — `@@gtid_binlog_state` is newest-per-domain (UNCHANGED across a PURGE, ground-truthed), and there is no `GTID_SUBSET`/`@@gtid_purged`; so a purged-position resume is refused LOUDLY via the reactive stream error 1236 (`isMariaDBPurgedGTIDError` → `ir.ErrPositionInvalid` → ADR-0022 cold-start), pinned on both LTS lines. `@@server_uuid` read skipped on MariaDB (no such var; GTID mode never uses it). The Phase-1 coded refusal (`SLUICE-E-CDC-MARIADB-UNSUPPORTED` / `ir.CDCUnsupportedExplainer`) is removed — every mysql-family flavor now supports CDC. Backup snapshot + incremental for MariaDB now route through the consistent-snapshot + GTID-position-capture path (an intended consequence of the CDCBinlog flip). **CONCURRENCY chunk — the binlog CDC streaming path — must land through CI's `-race` Integration job before any tag (Windows dev box is CGO=0).** CI: `mariadb:11.4` + `mariadb:10.11` CDC legs (basic convergence, resume-after-kill exactly-once, no-per-tx-churn, purged-position loud refusal) + a cross-engine `mariadb → postgres` `sync start` end-to-end pin (`TestStreamer_MariaDBToPostgres`: cold-start → CDC handoff → CRUD convergence → warm-resume, asserting JSON-identity + temporal fidelity through both bulk-copy AND CDC). The cross-engine leg caught two defects the reader-level pins could not — the warm-resume Bug-142 shape (source-retag stamps `Engine="mariadb"`, which `isMySQLFamilyEngine` rejected — FIXED, folded in) and the native-uuid/inet CDC gap below.
- **P3 native uuid / inet6 / inet4 through CDC — DECODE SHIPPED (ADR-0171), refusal lifted.** The Phase-3 refusal (`SLUICE-E-CDC-MARIADB-NATIVE-TYPE-UNSUPPORTED`, ADR-0170) is replaced by a faithful flavor-gated binlog decode. **The roadmap draft's premise was FALSIFIED by live ground truth on 11.4 + 10.11 (identical):** MariaDB does NOT reorder the uuid time fields — it stores **canonical big-endian** (`01234567-89ab-cdef-8123-456789abcdef` arrives as those bytes verbatim, no `UUID_TO_BIN` swap), so a straight hex format is correct. The real subtlety was **trailing-zero stripping**: MariaDB frames these as length-prefixed `CHAR`/`BINARY`, so the binlog delivers them with trailing `0x00` bytes removed (nil uuid / `0.0.0.0` / `::` arrive EMPTY; `2001:db8::` arrives 4 bytes) — the decode right-pads to the fixed width (16 uuid/inet6, 4 inet4; over-width refused loudly), and since a stripped inet6 can be ≤4 bytes the width comes from the declared `data_type` (`tableSchema.NativeKinds`), never `len(raw)`. inet6 text matches MariaDB's BSD `inet_ntop6` (`mariadbInet6Text`), NOT Go `netip` (they diverge on IPv4-compatible `::a.b.c.d`). CDC converges byte-for-byte with the bulk-copy driver text. Refusal fully removed (stream-start preflight, both snapshot openers, add-table `PreflightCDCScope`); `ir.CDCScopePreflighter` + the pipeline add-table hook kept as a generic extension point; the coded error retained-but-unused. Pinned: unit byte→text family × shape matrix; same-engine CDC value fidelity (src == driver text) on both LTS lines across INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; cross-engine `mariadb → postgres` (native uuid/inet ::text) and `mariadb → mysql` (the silent-corruption target now holds the exact value) through live CDC. **CONCURRENCY chunk — must land through CI's `-race` Integration before any tag.** Bulk migrate of these types was already unaffected (Phase 2).

- **Matrix expansion — SHIPPED (2026-07-17, item 73 follow-up).** The value-fidelity + CDC-forward-compat pins now run the full LTS spread **10.11 / 11.4 / 11.8 / 12.3** (was 10.11 + 11.4 only), directly closing ADR-0171's stated residual risk ("a new LTS line should be added to that matrix"). The native uuid/inet binlog byte layout was re-ground-truthed live and is **byte-identical on 11.8, 12.3, and the 13.1 preview** (uuid canonical big-endian; the four netip-divergent inet6 shapes render exactly as `mariadbInet6Text` targets) — no divergence, no code change. 12.3 additionally exercises MariaDB 12's `SHOW MASTER STATUS` → `SHOW BINLOG STATUS` situation live: both statements still work on 12.3.2 (the reader's `masterStatusSpellings` fallback lands on `SHOW MASTER STATUS`), and `SHOW BINARY LOG STATUS` is rejected 1064 on 11.x/12.x but now ACCEPTED on 13.1 — all handled by the existing fallback list, zero code change. **11.8 + 12.3 are REQUIRED** legs (the engines-mysql shard loops `mariadbLTSImages`); the **13.1 preview is a non-required `continue-on-error` leg** (`integration-mariadb-preview`, `mariadbpreview` build tag) using the moving quay.io devel tag, so a preview blip can never gate a merge. 11.8/12.3 are GHCR-mirrored (the `mirror_stock_refs` set) to avoid docker.io cold-pull flakiness; 13.1 is quay-only. **CONCURRENCY-adjacent (extends the CDC value-fidelity path) — the required legs land through CI's `-race` Integration before any tag.**

**Gotchas:** the flavor pattern fits (Vanilla/PlanetScale/Vitess precedent) but capabilities must be honest per phase; detection via `@@version` `-MariaDB` suffix is trivial and should refuse-loudly-by-default until P1 lands (today's errors are loud but incidental — make them intentional).

### 70. DigitalOcean Managed MySQL: the lying-retention trap — host-pattern preflight advisory + managed-services section (operator-flagged, live-probed 2026-07-15) — *(a)+(b) SHIPPED v0.99.253; (c) RDS half ANSWERED 2026-07-16 (see below), DO half unprobed*

Live probe (throwaway `db-s-1vcpu-1gb`, MySQL 8.4, 60 min): **every binlog file is purged ~13-16 minutes after creation on defaults** by an out-of-band platform reaper — while `@@binlog_expire_logs_seconds` reads **259200 (3 days)** and the DO config API shows NO retention field until first set. The variable lies; no SQL-level preflight can catch this host class. The PlanetScale-docs remedy is confirmed working: `PATCH /v2/databases/{id}/config {"config":{"binlog_retention_period":86400}}` (seconds, range 600–86400) — takes effect immediately, no restart, and the pre-existing binlogs stop being purged. sluice's cold copy + CDC handoff work against DO (needs the cluster CA from `GET /v2/databases/{id}/ca` via `--source-tls-ca`, ADR-0158; `doadmin` has replication grants), but sluice has **zero proactive retention warning** — the hazard is loud only AFTER loss (`ErrPositionInvalid` "binlog purged"), and with auto-resnapshot a >15-min cold copy becomes a **resnapshot livelock** (each retry re-copies, exceeds the window again).

- **(a) Host-pattern preflight advisory (S).** On MySQL sources matching `*.db.ondigitalocean.com`, WARN at sync/backup start: effective retention may be ~10-15 min regardless of `binlog_expire_logs_seconds`; name the `binlog_retention_period` config-API knob and the 86400 recommendation. Host-pattern is the ONLY reliable signal (the variable lies); note Aiven-hosted MySQL likely shares the behavior (same platform lineage).
- **(b) docs/managed-services.md DO MySQL section (S).** All of the above + the CA requirement + bonus gotchas: default `sql_mode` includes `ANSI` (double-quoted strings are identifiers) and `sql_require_primary_key=true`.
- **(c) Open question (unprobed, time-boxed out):** does an ATTACHED binlog-dump connection hold the purger back — i.e., is a live caught-up stream safe indefinitely at default retention, or only between purge ticks? Decides whether (a)'s advisory needs to fire for RUNNING streams too. **RDS answer (live-probed 2026-07-16, RDS MySQL 8.4.9 sibling probe): NO — an attached, caught-up stream does NOT hold the purger back** (sluice attached at `000005:466`; files 000005-000009 were purged on schedule while the stream ran; a caught-up stream survives only by sitting on the never-purgeable active file, and whether a *lagging* dump thread pins its mid-read file was not isolated — do not rely on it). So the advisory MUST apply to running streams, which the shipped shape satisfies (it fires at every sync/backup start, incl. warm resumes). The RDS advisory itself shipped detect-first (`mysql.rds_configuration` probe, host-gated on `*.rds.amazonaws.com` — see `internal/engines/mysql/host_advisories_rds.go`); the DO half of the question remains unprobed and DO's advisory stays unconditional.

- **(a) Pooler-endpoint preflight WARN (S).** The Neon `-pooler` host (pgbouncer transaction mode) survived a full snapshot-pinned parallel migrate at this scale, silently — but pinned server conns during long-lived snapshot transactions risk pool exhaustion mid-copy at higher parallelism/scale with a confusing failure. WARN when the source host matches a known pooler pattern (Neon `-pooler`, Supabase `pooler.`), recommending the direct endpoint.
- **(b) Provider-aware `wal_level` refusal remediation (S).** The refusal is loud and exact but its remedy ("set wal_level=logical in postgresql.conf and restart") is self-managed-only advice — on Neon the fix is the console/API `enable_logical_replication` toggle (irreversible, effective in seconds). Name `docs/postgres-source-prep.md` in the refusal + add provider hints there.
- **(c) Parallel-copy per-table completion INFO line (S, observability).** Tables above `--bulk-parallel-min-rows` complete SILENTLY at INFO — no `bulk copy complete` sibling for the within-table-parallel path (single-reader and raw-copy paths have one); only verify proves the copy. Related note: cold-start row estimates read `~0` on fresh branches (stale reltuples) — parallelism routing depends on stats freshness.
- **(d) docs/managed-services.md Neon section (S, docs).** Direct-vs-pooler endpoints; the `enable_logical_replication` API/console toggle (irreversible, seconds, no visible downtime); Neon's always-present internal `wal_proposer_slot` physical slot (slot-health correctly ignores it; any future slot-enumeration tooling must whitelist it); verify-full-vs-require sslmode interop; region co-location tip. Also record: autosuspend/cold-start unprobed (project stayed active) — an idle-then-migrate probe is the follow-up if resume-latency questions arise.

**Supabase leg (same day, second validation — bit-exact fidelity through BOTH Supavisor modes; CDC environment-blocked, not a sluice defect):**
- **(e) Pooler-aware CDC refusal (S — the highest-value fix of the two legs).** `sync start` through Supavisor fails with `syntax error at or near "CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT"` (SQLSTATE 42601) — the pooler strips `replication=database`, so the replication-protocol command reaches a normal backend as SQL. Loud, zero partial state, but reads like a sluice bug. Map that shape to: "the source appears to be a connection pooler (Supavisor/pgbouncer); logical replication requires the direct endpoint."
- **(f) AAAA-only resolve hint (S).** Supabase free-tier direct endpoints have ONLY an AAAA record (IPv4 is a paid add-on) — from an IPv4-only host sluice fails in 1s with Windows' cryptic `getaddrinfow: ... no data of the requested type`. On that resolve-failure class, probe for an AAAA record and say "host is IPv6-only; use the pooler endpoint (bulk migrate) or the IPv4 add-on (required for CDC — the pooler cannot proxy replication)".
- **(g) docs/managed-services.md Supabase section (S, docs).** IPv6-only direct endpoint (CDC impossible from IPv4-only networks without the add-on); session (:5432) vs transaction (:6543) pooler — bulk migrate works via session mode; transaction mode trips pgx's statement cache (42P05) and sluice's WARN + single-reader fallback completes correctly (parallel copy silently unavailable there — ties to (a)); `extra_float_digits=0` server default (text-level float comparisons lie — sluice's copy proven bit-exact via float8send; external diff tooling must pin `SET extra_float_digits=1`); platform schemas (auth/storage/realtime) correctly ignored by public scoping; `wal_level=logical` out of the box (contrast Neon).

### 68. Preflight gaps surfaced by the ps-discovery comparison (operator-flagged review 2026-07-15) — *(a)+(b) SHIPPED v0.99.253 (foreign-table WARN census + INHERITS refusal); (c)+(d)+(e) SHIPPED 2026-07-23 (large-object stranding WARN + slot/wal-sender headroom preflight + binlog_format=ROW gate); (f) remains filed*

PlanetScale's ps-discovery (v1.3.0) is a metadata CENSUS tool (verdicts live server-side in their Liftoff service; execution recommendations are pgdump/DMS) — complementary to sluice's verdicts-at-the-tool identity, and mildly validating (a ps-discovery user is a warm lead for sluice as the execution engine). But the comparison exposed checks it collects that sluice neither collects NOR enforces:

- **(a) Foreign tables are a SILENT SKIP today (S, silent-loss wart — fix soon).** `internal/engines/postgres/schema_reader.go:546` filters `table_type = 'BASE TABLE'`, so FDW foreign tables vanish from a migration with no signal — no WARN, no refusal, no test, no comment. Add a `relkind='f'` census and WARN-or-refuse naming the tables (the Bug-100 partition-refusal shape).
- **(b) Old-style (non-declarative) inheritance = the legacy twin of Bug 100 (S, silent-DUPLICATION class — fix soon).** Children are BASE TABLEs copied independently while a parent SELECT (no `ONLY`) also returns child rows. Probe `pg_inherits` where the parent is NOT `relkind='p'`; refuse like `partition_preflight.go`.
- **(c) Large-object stranding WARN (S). — SHIPPED 2026-07-23; named-suspect reachability fixed post-v0.99.292 (Bug 205).** Advisory census at migrate + sync preflight on PG sources: non-empty `pg_largeobject_metadata` + in-scope `oid`/`lo`-typed columns ⇒ WARN naming the suspect `table.column`s (with the carry recipes in type-mapping.md's "Postgres large objects" section); los with no in-scope suspects ⇒ one quieter WARN-and-proceed. The census runs BEFORE the schema read: an in-scope `oid`/`lo` column is itself an unsupported column type the schema read refuses loudly (it does NOT copy as a plain integer — the v0.99.292 wording drifted there), so the named WARN is the refusal's context and would be dead code after it. Probe failure skips silently (advisory — no new failure mode).
- **(d) Slot/sender headroom preflight (S). — SHIPPED 2026-07-23.** Probes `max_replication_slots` vs `pg_replication_slots` and `max_wal_senders` vs `pg_stat_replication` before a fresh slot-creating cold start; a full server refuses UPFRONT with the coded `SLUICE-E-CDC-REPLICATION-HEADROOM` naming usage/ceiling/each existing slot + the free-a-leftover remedies (`slot list`, `sync decommission`, `slot drop`) — instead of the raw mid-cold-start 53400. Cold-start only (warm/interrupted-COPY resume reuse their slot and never probe — integration-pinned at the ceiling); a failed census WARNs and continues (managed-PG permission variance must not invent a new hard failure); capability-gated to `ir.CDCLogicalReplication` (excludes postgres-trigger + MySQL).
- **(e) MySQL `binlog_format=ROW` upfront gate (S — verify current behavior first). — SHIPPED 2026-07-23; premise CONFIRMED by Phase-A ground truth.** Real mysql:8.0 with `--binlog-format=STATEMENT`: cold copy lands, then every live DML is SILENTLY LOST — QueryEvents hit the dispatcher's generic-DDL arm (nothing applied), the target freezes at the copy snapshot, the persisted position never advances, Run stays green and exits 0. The filed "quietly EMPTY CDC stream" premise held exactly (it neither errors nor partially delivers). Gate shipped: `preflightBinlogFormat` refuses `binlog_format != ROW` (STATEMENT and MIXED — MIXED statement-logs deterministic writes and is MariaDB's DEFAULT) with the coded `SLUICE-E-CDC-BINLOG-FORMAT-NOT-ROW` at the same three chokepoints as the Bug-193 row-image preflight (StreamChanges + both snapshot openers, so a cold start refuses BEFORE the bulk copy). Binlog flavors only (MariaDB shares the path and the variable — integration-pinned); VStream never takes this path (vtgate owns the row-event contract); bulk-only runs not gated. Residual (documented at the preflight): a SUPER session-level STATEMENT override still slips past the global read — those QueryEvents are ignored, an inherent limit sluice does not belt because executing SQL text against the target is not faithful CDC.
- **(f, opt-in advisory) Row-size/TOAST sampler pointed at TARGET limits** — borrow ps-discovery's `TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI` + `pg_column_size` FILTER + `attstorage` implementation (their data_size_analyzer) to predict oversized-row mid-copy failures against PS statement/chunk guidance and D1 caps.
- Docs note: managed-services.md PS-PG section can acknowledge the ps-discovery workflow ("ran ps-discovery? here's what sluice enforces automatically"). Their extension-dependency queries (`pg_depend` over `pg_extension`) could enrich the extension-refusal messages.

### 67. ADR-0148 revival: deploy-request index fallback for the errno-3024 wall (operator circle-back 2026-07-15) — *M; the 2026-07-02 deferral's costs have shrunk — the client/poller/freshness-gate now exist (ADR-0162) — and the design simplifies to REQUIRE-safe-migrations-on, no toggle machinery* — **✅ SHIPPED v0.99.255**

> **STATUS: SHIPPED v0.99.255 (2026-07-15).** Shipped as designed: automatic fallback on errno 3024 + errno-1105 direct-DDL-disabled at both deferred-build call sites, require-safe-migrations-on (never toggled; unavailable ⇒ the original error + the existing `--upfront-indexes` hint, unchanged), arming via new `migrate` flags `--planetscale-org`/`--planetscale-database`(DSN-derived)/`--planetscale-branch`/token env pair/`--planetscale-deploy-timeout`, per-table one-branch-one-DR batching of every still-pending index DDL, the conservative 64 GiB DATA_LENGTH skip-the-doomed-attempt probe, and the ADR-0162 freshness gate by composing the shared ADR-0165 `legRunner` (converged post-rebase onto the item-66 extraction). Error surfaces reuse `SLUICE-E-INDEX-STATEMENT-TIME-LIMIT` / `SLUICE-E-PS-DEPLOY-REQUEST-FAILED`. Full decisions in ADR-0148 §Implementation. **REVISED 2026-07-30 after a 122 GB field run (ADR-0148 §Revision):** `--planetscale-deploy-timeout` now defaults to `0` = wait for the deploy to reach a terminal state (the 1 h default gave up at ~29 % of a 106 GB / 153 M-row build, making the non-terminal exit the DEFAULT outcome at scale), the poller classifies PlanetScale's whole documented 20-value `deployment_state` enum so terminal failures still fail fast unbounded, progress / ETA / throttling / queue-pause / approval are narrated, the in-flight deployment's dev branch is left alone instead of asked to be deleted, and a non-terminal exit is the new `SLUICE-E-PS-DEPLOY-REQUEST-INCOMPLETE` rather than `…-FAILED`. Multi-table deploy-request queueing was investigated and rejected with evidence (PlanetScale serialises deployments per target branch — fan-out saves ~0.4 % and risks a documented queue wedge).

**Why revive.** The deferral's "heavy lift" was the control-plane machinery — now shipped (shared `internal/planetscale/api` client, tolerant DR poller, skip-revert, and the stale-branch freshness gate, which ANSWERS ADR-0148's open question about branch-off-a-freshly-migrated-table semantics: branches CAN come up stale and the rebase-via-backup guard handles it). The remaining wart was safe-migrations toggling; the ADR-0162 posture dissolves it: the fallback engages ONLY when safe migrations is already ON (+ service token present) — refuse/hint otherwise, never toggle. Operator note: with safe migrations increasingly the assumed PS posture, the fallback's precondition is the common case, and on such branches the DIRECT deferred `ALTER ... ADD INDEX` isn't just walled at ~900 s — it's refused outright (1105), so today those migrations end with a hint instead of an index.

**Speed expectations (state them honestly — the operator's prior test found this slow, and it inherently is):** the direct attempt burns up to ~900 s before the fallback engages (skip-the-doomed-attempt via a `DATA_LENGTH` probe is the recorded optional optimization — include it this time; on a 1105-refused branch the "attempt" fails instantly, no burn); the DR deploy itself is VReplication — real wall-clock on large tables, but async, unbounded by errno 3024, and narrated via the ADR-0162 poller with `--deploy-timeout` + resume guidance. The fallback's value is UNBLOCKING (index lands on already-copied data with no re-copy and no `--upfront-indexes` 11× load penalty), not speed. Prior findings preserved in ADR-0148; update its status line when this ships.

Pre-v5 chains restore byte-identically (version-gated legacy path; pinned); pre-v5 encrypted RESUME inherits the unbound shape. Tamper matrix + per-family crypto/codec pins landed. Residual (documented, out of scope): the manifest is unsigned — whole-backup rollback / tail truncation need a signed-manifest design. N-9's real-AKV live pin remains open (unit-level fake reproduces the no-version-metadata semantics; validate against real AKV before relying on it in anger). *Original why:* the encrypted-backup path currently provides confidentiality only, while two in-code comments and SECURITY.md's shared-storage framing imply integrity that doesn't exist. Verified: `gcm.Seal(nonce, nonce, plaintext, nil)` / `gcm.Open(nil, nonce, ct, nil)` — nil AAD (`internal/crypto/envelope.go:294,320`); zero KMS `EncryptionContext` anywhere in `internal/crypto`; `ChunkReader.Header()` has no non-test callers despite `pipeline/blobcodec/backup_chunk.go:50-56` claiming a column-rename "surfaces as a header mismatch on restore"; `Manifest.SchemaHash` is computed+written at 3 sites and compared nowhere despite `ir/backup/manifest.go:454-459` claiming chain-restore uses it as a tamper sanity check. Per-chain mode shares one CEK, so any valid chunk decrypts wherever a rewritten manifest points — chunk splice/rollback/omission on shared storage. *What:* GCM AAD = BackupID + chunk index; KMS EncryptionContext on wrap/unwrap; actually validate the chunk header on restore; actually compare SchemaHash in chain-restore — as one FormatVersion-bumping design. **Fixing the two lying comments is part of this item** (at minimum, if the integrity work is re-deferred, correct the comments to say what the code does). Grouped in: **N-9** — Azure Key Vault unwrap targets the *latest* key version and discards the WrapKey response `KID` (`internal/crypto/azure_kms.go:263-285`; the in-code comment asserts Azure recovers the wrap-time version from blob metadata — that is AWS/GCP behavior, Azure KW ciphertext carries none), so enabling key auto-rotation (common policy) makes restores of older chains fail with a misleading "wrong key or tampered". Persist the WrapKey response KID as the unwrap target. *Gotchas:* existing chains must keep restoring (Bug 116's FormatVersion loud-refusal discipline); per-chunk vs per-chain CEK modes differ in splice exposure; N-9 is derived from Azure API semantics, not live-run — pin against real AKV (or a recorded fixture) before shipping.

So the unconditional recovery decoders are correct in every reachable mode, and the audit's proposed fix (threading sqlMode into the decode) would itself have corrupted (`'C:\\temp'` read "raw" under NBE → two backslashes). Landed instead: the live family × mode pin `TestSchemaLiteralDecode_SQLModeMatrix_ByteExact` (mysql engine integration; binary defaults quoted+hex, ENUM+SET labels, table comment incl. NUL-recovery, column comment, VARCHAR default — each under {default, NBE} reader sessions via the real `WithSQLMode` plumbing, session mode asserted on the reader's own connection), plus the named invariant ("mode-independent print discipline") in `binary_default_recovery.go` / `types.go` / `connect.go` so nobody "completes" the one-sided fix later. The pin fails loudly if a future MySQL starts printing mode-dependently.

PlanetScale/Vitess flavors default `interpolateParams=true` at the `parseDSNForFlavor` choke point; vanilla stays binary (deliberate; DSN opt-in documented in throughput-tuning); explicit DSN wins (raw-DSN explicitness detection); NBE ground-truthed correct in-driver (pinned, no guard); unsafe-collation default steps aside with WARN; packet headroom pinned (driver ErrSkip → prepared fallback at the boundary). Two INFO-grade residuals from the round-2 fidelity review, carried here so they don't vanish: (G4) ~~the VStream COPY/CDC path decodes FLOAT through its OWN gRPC field carrier — entirely outside the SQL read projection this chunk fixed — pre-existing and unaudited for the same float32-carrier precision class (informational; audit if a VStream FLOAT fidelity report ever surfaces)~~ **RESOLVED by vttestserver ground truth (2026-07-09, `TestVStream_FloatCarrierParity`): the CDC (binlog row-event) leg is float32-EXACT — vttablet re-encodes the binlog float32 bits as shortest-round-trip text (`'E', -1, 32`), so only the float64 carrier's low bits differ from the SQL reader's float64(float32(x)), observable solely by a double-width target — the informational, confirmed and pinned at the float32-exactness bar; the COPY leg, however, surfaced a REAL float32-level silent loss (mysqld display rounding), promoted to its own open-bugs entry (2026-07-09) below**; and the pgtrigger string-"NaN" bypass documented in ADR-0153 (loud, non-retriable, just less well-named). Setup no longer creates them and emits idempotent `DROP INDEX IF EXISTS` for both names so any pre-existing install converges on the next setup run (no schema_version migration — pre-production simplification per operator). The capture trigger's per-fired-row PK catalog lookup is replaced by the ADR-0066 §3 TG_ARGV[0] JSON-array bake (composite PKs in conkey order); a stale bake after a post-setup PK ALTER refuses writes loudly via a projection guard (the event-trigger tier already refuses at the ALTER's op='X' row). - ~~**N-14 — `--rebuild-catalog` stamps `DefaultCodec` on rebuilt lineage regardless of actual chunk compression (wrong-heal on the DR path).**~~ — **IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-09; released v0.99.204).** The rebuilt record's codec is now SNIFFED from chunk magic bytes and VERIFIED across the chain (`blobcodec.SniffCodec` + `lineage.SniffChainCodec` — one probe per manifest; the sniff is deterministic because a chunk's codec input always begins with the header line's `{`, so zstd `28 B5 2F FD` / gzip `1F 8B` / none `{` are disjoint). Sniff-and-verify posture on the durable-record path (`RebuildLineageCatalogAt`): mixed probes, unknown magic, truncated/unreadable chunks all REFUSE loudly. Chunk-layout finding that shaped the encrypted leg: the codec sits INSIDE the encryption envelope (`ChunkWriter` compresses then encrypts on Close), so encrypted chunks carry no codec magic on disk — a keyless rebuild refuses (wraps `lineage.ErrCodecSniffEncrypted`, steering to `--encrypt`) and a keyed rebuild decrypts one chunk (same `UnwrapChainCEK`/AAD chokepoints as restore) and sniffs the plaintext; `backup verify --rebuild-catalog` builds the read envelope from the existing `EncryptionFlags`. `ResolveLineage`'s synthetic root gets the same sniff, best-effort (its result is in-memory, re-derived per call — on probe failure/encrypted-without-keys it WARNs naming the DefaultCodec assumption instead of hard-failing, so keyless flows like SHA-only verify keep working; a wrong assumption still fails loudly at first chunk decode). DefaultCodec survives only as the nothing-to-probe (chunk-less chain) fallback, WARN-named on both paths. Pinned: magic-table + every-codec-family real-writer bytes + encrypted-layout unit pins (blobcodec), rebuild/synthetic family pins + mixed-codec refusal + truncated refusal + encrypted keyless-refuse/keyed-sniff (lineage), and the DR scenario end-to-end per codec family incl. the encrypted leg (`TestBackupRebuildCatalog_*`, pipeline integration). *Original why:* `pipeline/lineage/chain_catalog.go` recorded `blobcodec.DefaultCodec` (zstd) never-sniffed on rebuild and on the synthetic root, and restore trusts the record — a gzip/none-era chain whose `lineage.json` was lost got a rebuilt catalog that lied, and restore failed with a bare zstd decode error whose remediation hint pointed back at the same rebuild tool.
- ✅ **FIXED (in review, 2026-07-09) — N-17 — testing-guard blind spots beyond the known manifest drift.** (a) `check-run-filter-coverage.sh` now auto-discovers the tag-axis set from `*_test.go` `//go:build` lines (vet-tags-style GOOS/GOARCH stripping) and fails on any tag with neither a MANIFEST axis nor a documented `EXEMPT_TAGS` entry (psverify/jsonbench/compressbench, each with a rationale in the header; a stale exemption also fails) — a future `integration && newtag` suite can no longer type-check, pass both coverage guards, and run in no workflow. Plus the hand-copied-mirror tripwire: every MANIFEST regex must appear verbatim (fixed-string grep) in the workflow file its leg label names, so a `-run` filter edited on one side fails the Lint job (documented limitation: a stale regex surviving in a YAML comment could mask drift; full YAML parsing wasn't worth it in a POSIX-sh guard). (b) `check-shard-coverage.sh`'s matching now mirrors ci.yml's actual package listing — bare entries (`internal/pipeline`, `internal/pipeline/backup`) are NON-recursive like the `./pkg/` go-test arguments; `/...` entries cover subtrees — pinned by an always-run `self_test` whose load-bearing case asserts `internal/pipeline` does NOT cover `internal/pipeline/migcore` (verified latent at fix time: no integration tests exist under any pipeline subpackage except the guarded set). Both (a) and (b) were also proven by staged fake-escapee negative runs. (c) The `kmsverify` scaffolding is wired for real: round-trip, chain extension (the Bug-43 salt hazard has no KMS analog — the same envelope extends the chain, no rebuild hook), and the wrong-key + missing-key loud refusals now run against a real localstack KMS container + real PG under `integration && kmsverify`, with a weekly + dispatch `kmsverify` leg in extended-suites.yml and a matching run-filter-guard MANIFEST axis; only the IAM access-denied case remains an honest skip (localstack community edition doesn't enforce IAM — that branch stays unit-pinned in `internal/crypto/aws_kms_test.go`).
- ~~**N-11 — fleet zero-coercion defeats the documented "0 disables" semantics (the zero-value-collapse class on the fleet layer).**~~ — **IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-09; released v0.99.204).** The full `firstNonZero*` audit of the fleet spec→Streamer mapping classified every coerced field: class (a) — 0 is documented-meaningful on the CLI (`--apply-exec-timeout` / `--heartbeat-interval` "0 disables"; `--max-buffer-bytes=0` = no orchestrator cap, engine default) — `max-buffer-bytes` / `apply-exec-timeout` / `heartbeat-interval` are now POINTER-typed in `SyncSpec` (nil = key omitted → the `sync start` flag default via the new `orDefault` helper; an explicit 0 passes through as 0, byte-identical to the flag; YAML key names unchanged); the `apply-retry-attempts`/`-backoff-base`/`-backoff-cap` trio is pointer-typed for the REFUSAL side of the same class (nil = omitted → ADR-0038 defaults; an explicit value INCLUDING 0 reaches `validateRetryFlags` verbatim and is refused with the CLI's exact out-of-range message, instead of being silently absorbed into the default); only the restart `backoff-base`/`backoff-cap` stay value-typed (`RestartPolicy.withDefaults` documents zero-as-unset and there is no CLI counterpart; the `printFleetPlan` coercion is display-only), with in-code comments. Pinned through the REAL parsers per the Bug-180 lesson: `TestFleetZeroDisables_ThroughLoadPath_N11` ({omitted → default; explicit `0` and `0s` → 0/disabled; non-zero → verbatim} × each "0 disables" field through `loadFleetConfig`), `TestFleetRetryZeroRefused_ThroughLoadPath_N11` (explicit `apply-retry-*: 0` refused through the load path with the CLI-identical message; omitted → defaults; in-range → verbatim), `TestSyncStartFleetParity_ExplicitZero_N11` (kong-parsed `sync start` explicit-0 and defaults produce the SAME Streamer values as the fleet keys), `TestSyncSpecFingerprint_ZeroVsOmitted_N11` (explicit 0 ≠ omitted under the SIGHUP-reload fingerprint, so flipping between them restarts the sync). *Original:* `cmd/sluice/sync_run.go:783-791` coerced `apply-exec-timeout: 0` / `heartbeat-interval: 0` / `max-buffer-bytes: 0` to the 60s/60s/64MiB defaults via `firstNonZero*`, while the flag help documents "0 disables" and `sync start` passes an explicit 0 through — "unset" and "explicit 0" were conflated for fleet specs only.
- ✅ **FIXED (in review, 2026-07-08) — pgtrigger cold-start anchor: in-flight-txn rows are MVCC-invisible to the anchor query (epoch-INDEPENDENT hole; live-confirmed 2026-07-08 during the N-1 xid8 fix).** `readChangeLogAnchor`'s `MIN(id)-1` hold-down arm can only see *visible* rows — a change-log row inserted by a still-open transaction is invisible to the anchor's snapshot, so when that txn's already-allocated id was lower than every visible not-yet-settled row, the anchor landed above it (repro: A inserts change-log id=1 open, B inserts id=2 committed → anchor 1, gap-free needs 0; the loss reproduced end-to-end through the real Streamer cold start — row missing on target, exit 0). **Fix (three-phase; Phase-A failing pins written first):** `OpenSnapshotStream` now exports the copy snapshot's visibility horizon from the pinned conn, assigns a txid upper bound on the pool (`pg_current_xact_id()`), waits for every pre-bound transaction to settle (fresh snapshot per poll; 5-min budget → loud refusal naming the stuck txids + pg_stat_activity remedy), then clamps the anchor below `MIN(id)` of change-log rows not `pg_visible_in_snapshot` in the horizon. **The candidate sketch here (pg_snapshot_xip alone) proved UNSOUND during Phase A** — snapshot xmax is latestCompletedXid+1, so the only running txn sits at/above xmax outside every xip list (live-probed `744:744:`); the shipped wait unions snapshot xmin (oldest still-running) with xip under the assigned bound. Invariant + case split documented on `waitForPreSnapshotTxnsToSettle` and in ADR-0066 impl-notes. Pins: `TestSnapshotStream_InFlightTxnAnchor_NoGap`, `TestPGTriggerStreamer_InFlightTxnSpansColdStart_NoLoss` (both mutation-verified: fail with the clamp disabled), `TestSettleWait_TimeoutRefusesLoudly`, `TestSettleWait_QuiescentSourceFirstPollExits` + query-shape unit pins. The narrower steady-state cousin (xid-assignment order can invert change-log-id order across multi-statement txns — inherent to the ADR's Debezium-style design; the safety-lag hold-back bounds it) is UNCHANGED and remains open.

### Open bugs awaiting fix windows

Tracked in detail in the project's internal regression catalog; recap here for roadmap visibility:

- ~~**VStream COPY silently display-rounds FLOAT columns (found 2026-07-09 ground-truthing the ADR-0153 G4 residual; MED-HIGH, silent-precision class, PlanetScale/Vitess sources only):**~~ **FIXED (2026-07-09; released in the v0.99.206–207 pair) — post-COPY exact SQL re-read, EXACT by default on BOTH consumers.** Root cause: vttablet's rowstreamer issues a bare-column SELECT over the text protocol, so the wire bytes are mysqld's own FLOAT rendering (the exact bug class ADR-0153's `(col * 1E0)` projection fixed on the SQL reader — but that SELECT is built inside vttablet, un-injectable client-side, so the *reader stays rounded by design*; the fix lives one layer up). Ground truth on vttestserver mysql80: `8388608` → `8388610`, float32-max → a different float32, `-123456.789` → `-123457`. The CDC leg is float32-exact (pinned), DOUBLE + `-0.0` exact on both legs (pinned). **Fix:** a new `ir.LossyFloatCopyReader` gate (the VStream cold-start reader returns true) + an `ir.FloatRepairWriter` target surface (MySQL + PG). **Sync cold-start** (`internal/pipeline/streamer_coldstart_float_repair.go`): after the bulk-copy completes and BEFORE the CDC anchor is persisted, re-read every repairable table's single-precision FLOAT columns EXACTLY from the source over a separate SQL connection (`Engine.OpenRowReader` → the `(col*1E0)` projection) and UPDATE the target rows by PK; CDC then replays from the copy anchor forward, so any value that changed in the re-read window is re-applied to its final value (exact + eventually-consistent). **Backup** (`internal/pipeline/backup/float_repair.go`): also EXACT by default — a `floatExactPatchReader` wraps the snapshot reader, building a per-table PK→exact-floats map and patching each COPY row's FLOAT columns before archiving (a bounded merge-join is infeasible: the VStream COPY stream is NOT PK-ordered — Vitess scans by a cheaper unique key than the PK and re-emits catchup rows out of order, so there's no monotonic key to merge on). The map is **BOUNDED-memory**: capped at `--float-reread-max-rows` (default 2M rows; serial VStream sweep → one table at a time), and a table over the cap **falls back loudly** (default: WARN + rounded; `--strict-float`: refuse) rather than OOM-ing on a huge FLOAT table (ADR-0071 tenet). Cost = a bounded within-row temporal skew that self-heals on a chain restore (incrementals replay from the full's `EndPosition` forward); position/VGTID untouched. **Escape hatches (both paths):** `--no-float-exact-reread` (opt-out → rounded-but-perfectly-consistent) and `--strict-float` (refuse loudly, `SLUICE-E-VSTREAM-FLOAT-LOSSY`, exit 3). Keyless / float-PK-only tables can't be re-read → WARN-only rounded (or refuse under `--strict-float`). `TestVStream_FloatCarrierParity`'s skipped sub-test is converted to a reader-still-rounds ground-truth pin (the reader is unfixable); the target-exactness pins live at the pipeline layer (`TestStreamer_FloatRepair_*_VStream_PG`) + the writer/patch/plan unit + integration tests. Concurrency-critical (cold-start→CDC handoff ordering): the `-race` Integration + vstream jobs must gate the tag.
- ~~**`TestStreamer_PostgresToPostgres_BatchedApply` threshold flake (2026-07-09; LOW, CI-noise class)**~~ — **FIXED (2026-07-09; released in the v0.99.206–207 pair), as the mechanism assertion the entry prescribed.** The pg_stat_database commit-delta constant (`<= 52`) is gone; the test now observes every coalesced flush through a new pipeline test seam (`batchApplyObserverForTest`, an [ir.BatchObserver] installed on the applier when the AIMD controller doesn't take the seat; onTableCopiedObserver disposition) and asserts the MECHANISM: every source row flowed through an observed flush AND mean rows/flush >= 10 (per-change apply yields mean exactly 1 — the per-change Apply path bypasses the batch loop and its observer entirely, so both assertions fail against it by an order of magnitude; healthy run = 2-3 flushes of ~100). The test pins ApplyConcurrency=1 (the seam watches the serial ADR-0092 batch loop; the ADR-0104 lane path reports to per-lane controllers and has its own suites). No timing-dependent constant remains. *Original:* flaked once on a loaded `-race` runner — 200 source rows landed in 55 dest commits vs the pinned `<= 52`; the assertion counted DEST COMMIT deltas, which depend on change-arrival timing against the coalescing window.
- **UNIQUE-constraint attribute fidelity (2026-07-04, from the TRIAGE-#4 review; LOW-MED, silent-weaker class): ✅ WARN half SHIPPED (v0.100 readiness C3, 2026-07-24) — faithful carry remains the follow-up.** `DEFERRABLE` (`pg_constraint.condeferrable`), PG-15 `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (stored on `pg_index.indnullsnotdistinct` — the entry's original `connullsnotdistinct` column never existed; a real PG-16 read 42703'd it), and PG-18 `WITHOUT OVERLAPS` (`pg_constraint.conperiod`; PG-17 reverted temporal constraints pre-GA) are now READ (version-gated so older servers never 42703), carried on `ir.Index` (`ConstraintDeferrable`/`ConstraintNullsNotDistinct`/`ConstraintWithoutOverlaps`, riding the backup wire), and a loud one-time WARN per affected constraint fires at schema-read time naming the attribute and the plain-UNIQUE weaker landing; the dump-parity oracle carries a cited `customers_extref_nnd` NULLS-NOT-DISTINCT cell that goes stale-loud when the carry ships. **Follow-up (the M version, still open):** (a) faithful same-engine PG → PG carry — emit the attributes in `emitAddUniqueConstraint` and drop the WARN + allowlist entry for that pair; (b) the plain-`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... NULLS NOT DISTINCT` sibling (PG 15+ allows the attribute on bare unique indexes too; `indnullsnotdistinct` is index-side, so a non-constraint-backed unique index also lands weaker today, un-WARNed — needs an index-level IR field next to `Unique`, not the constraint-attribute trio).
- **Sequence-carry review residuals (2026-07-03, both LOW, loud-not-silent):** (a) `primeOneStandaloneSequence`'s never-called canonicalization (`srcLast = Value − Increment`) can push the cutover prime past the *inner* bound when `Increment > margin` (e.g. `START 1000 INCREMENT 5000`, never called) — `setval` errors and cutover fails loudly with a raw PG bounds error; clamping applyValue into `[MinValue, MaxValue]` on both sides would turn the confusing abort into a correct prime. (b) Mid-stream `ALTER SEQUENCE` option changes (e.g. INCREMENT) produce no SchemaDelta (`diffSchemas` is table-only, pre-existing) — the new end-of-window refresh *records* the changed options in the newest link but the chain-tail re-prime only setvals, never ALTERs, so option drift is recorded-but-unapplied on a restored target.
- **Identity sequences go stale at chain-restore tail** (found 2026-07-03 during the item-51 sequence-carry review; live-reproduced: `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "orders_pkey" (SQLSTATE 23505)` on the first post-restore insert). ✅ **FIXED 2026-07-04 (replay-path hardening chunk):** `ChainRestore.Run` step 5 now calls `syncIdentitySequencesAtTail` right beside the item-51 standalone-sequence re-prime — the newest link's schema snapshot, retargeted + filtered like the base full's restore, through the required `ir.SchemaWriter.SyncIdentitySequences` surface (engine-neutral: no-op on MySQL/SQLite) under the ADR-0114 reparent retry. Idempotent, data-derived MAX+1; the broker's `--reset-target-data` ChainRestore inherits it. Pinned by `TestBackup_ChainRestore_IdentitySequenceSyncedAtTail` (the exact 23505 repro, first post-restore insert must draw max+1) + `TestChainRestore_IdentitySequencesSyncedAtTail_Dispatch` (unit: sync runs twice — base full + tail, tail last).
- **SYSTEMIC — cross-engine out-of-range / invalid values silently transformed (4 vectors)** (found 2026-06-08, rig systemic sweep of v0.99.18; rig `FINDING-systemic-out-of-range-silent-loss.md`). A value the target can't faithfully hold is silently clamped/truncated/normalized to a wrong-but-plausible value with exit 0, instead of refused. **Operator decisions (2026-06-08):** Vector A → refuse loudly by default + opt-in `--zero-date={error,null,epoch}`; Vector D → keep TINYINT(1)→bool but WARN on non-{0,1} + add integer override tokens.
  - **Vector A (CRITICAL, default path, ✅ FIXED v0.99.19):** MySQL invalid/zero/partial dates (`0000-00-00`, `YYYY-00-00`, `YYYY-MM-00`) silently normalized to wrong dates (e.g. `2026-00-00`→`2025-11-30`). Root: `cfg.ParseTime=true` (`connect.go:205`) → go-sql-driver parses partial dates via `time.Date` (which normalizes) *before* sluice's `decodeTime` sees them, so the original is lost. **Fix shipped:** rather than flip `ParseTime` (TZ-risky), the read path reads `DATE`/`DATETIME`/`TIMESTAMP` via `CAST(... AS CHAR)` (`selectColumnExpr`, used by both `buildSelect` and `buildBatchedSelect`) so `decodeTime` validates the raw string. Zero/partial dates surface as a `*zeroDateValueError` sentinel, resolved at the reader sites (which hold `col.Nullable`) by `applyZeroDatePolicy` per `--zero-date={error,null,epoch}` (default `error`). `SetZeroDateMode` mirrors `sessionSQLMode`. Pinned: full temporal class × every zero shape × each policy (unit) + live-driver normalization ground-truth (integration, real MySQL 8.0). Behavior change: `0000-00-00` previously → NULL silently, now refused by default (`--zero-date=null` restores). Docs: `migrating-legacy-mysql.md` §1, `value-types.md`. **Value-fidelity review follow-ups (2026-06-08):** (1) ✅ FIXED — the `CAST(... AS CHAR) AS \`c\`` projection aliases a temporal PK to its bare name, so `buildBatchedSelect`'s `ORDER BY \`c\`` bound the CHAR alias (string sort) while the keyset predicate `(\`c\`) > (?)` compared the date column; correct only by ISO lexical monotonicity and it forced a filesort. Now both clauses are table-qualified (`\`tbl\`.\`c\``) → date-typed, index-ordered; pinned by a SQL-shape unit test + DATE/DATETIME(6)-PK pagination integration tests + a chunked-path zero-date integration test. (2) ✅ FIXED v0.99.19 — **VStream parity:** the PlanetScale/Vitess CDC parser `parseVStreamDateTime` (`cdc_vstream.go`) now detects zero/partial dates via the shared `isMySQLZeroDate` and returns the `*zeroDateValueError` sentinel (instead of a generic `time.Parse` error → raw `[]byte` passthrough → confusing downstream failure). `decodeVStreamCell` surfaces the sentinel as the cell value (it has no error channel); `decodeVStreamRow` resolves it via `applyZeroDatePolicy` — refuse (default) errors the stream loudly naming the column, null carries SQL NULL (refused on a NOT NULL field, derived from `query.Field.Flags` NOT_NULL with assume-nullable fallback), epoch substitutes the representable floor. Covers the live CDC reader + the cold-start COPY + CDC catch-up paths. Pinned: `TestDecodeVStreamCell_ZeroDateSentinel` (family × zero shapes; valid→time.Time; malformed→[]byte) + `TestDecodeVStreamRow_ZeroDatePolicy` (refuse/null/epoch/NOT-NULL). `--zero-date` now behaves identically on the vanilla MySQL and PlanetScale/Vitess source paths.
  - **Vector D (HIGH, default path, ALL directions incl same-engine, ✅ FIXED v0.99.21):** MySQL `TINYINT(1)` mapped to bool at the IR read layer → non-{0,1} values (2/127/−1/−128) silently collapsed to true/false, corrupting even MySQL→MySQL. **Fix shipped:** kept the `TINYINT(1)`→bool default (documented MySQL convention) but the bulk-copy / snapshot read path now DETECTS any value ∉ {0,1} and WARNs loudly **once per column** (`boolRangeWarner` in `bool_range_warn.go`, gated in `RowReader.stream`; pure detector `tinyBoolOutOfRange` in `value_decode.go`), naming the `table.column` + an example value + the `--type-override` remedy. Added `smallint`/`integer`/`int` target-type tokens (`translate/mappings.go` registry → `ir.Integer{16/32}`); the override rewrites the IR type the **reader** decodes with, so the cell is read as an integer (not collapsed) and preserved end-to-end — `smallint` is the safe floor (a `tinyint` override would re-emit `TINYINT(1)` and re-trigger the bool mapping). Pinned: `tinyBoolOutOfRange` purity + warn-once unit tests; token resolution; an end-to-end integration test (MySQL→PG default warns+collapses; MySQL→PG **and** same-engine MySQL→MySQL override preserves real SMALLINT values). Docs: `type-mapping.md`, `value-types.md`. **WARN coverage now spans ALL read paths (v0.99.21 follow-up landed):** the copy/snapshot reader (`RowReader.stream`), the binlog CDC reader (`decodeBinlogRow`, via a `boolWarn` on `CDCReader`), and the VStream CDC + cold-start-COPY path (`decodeVStreamRow`, via a `boolWarn` on `vstreamCDCReader` / `vstreamSnapshotStream`; VStream cells are text-encoded so the detector re-parses the literal). Each warner is per-reader, warn-once-per-`table.column`, nil-safe. Pinned by `TestDecodeBinlogRow_TinyInt1OutOfRangeWarns` + `TestDecodeVStreamRow_TinyInt1OutOfRangeWarns`. No remaining Vector-D detection gap.
  - **Vector B (HIGH, requires `--mysql-sql-mode=''`): ✅ FIXED v0.99.28.** Overflow/over-long/out-of-range on a MySQL-target write under `--mysql-sql-mode=''` → silent clamp/truncate. **Ground-truthed** (rig MySQL): under `sql_mode=''` the value silently clamps (300→127, 'toolong'→'too', 99999→999) but MySQL STILL flags it on the warning list (`@@warning_count`/`SHOW WARNINGS`) — so the "non-strict suppresses the warnings" assumption was wrong; the signal is there, the prior code just SKIPPED checking it under relaxed mode. **Fix:** `reportBulkWriteWarnings` (`load_data_writer.go`) now, under relaxed mode, emits a loud **one-time-per-table WARN** (not a refusal — the operator opted into coercion) naming the coercions + the `--type-override` remedy, instead of the silent skip; under strict mode it still refuses. Wired into ALL THREE bulk-write paths (the Bug-74 path-family lesson — a value-fidelity review BLOCK caught that the first cut covered only two): LOAD DATA (`writeLoadData`), the batched-INSERT path (`writeBatched`, used when `local_infile=OFF`/geometry), AND the idempotent upsert path (`writeBatchedIdempotent`, used on **resume / parallel chunked copy >100k / add-table / VStream cold-start** — the path most large migrations take). Each pins a single conn so the session-scoped `SHOW WARNINGS` is reliable; the idempotent path checks before advancing the durable watermark so a strict-mode refusal can't mark a clamped batch durable. **Bonus:** reading `SHOW WARNINGS` FIRST (the old code read `@@warning_count` first, which clears the list) fixes the empty-`Examples: []` cosmetic bug in the strict-mode refusal AND the NaN/±Inf refusal. Pinned: `TestLoadDataWarning_RelaxedModeWarnsNotRefuses` + `TestWriteBatched_RelaxedModeWarnsOnClamp` + `TestWriteBatchedIdempotent_RelaxedModeWarnsOnClamp` (clamp 300→127 + WARN, once-per-table) + the strict refuse pin retained. **Remaining (minor, not a bulk-copy gap):** the CDC applier write path (steady-state out-of-range under relaxed mode) doesn't yet run this check; all THREE migrate/cold-start bulk-copy paths — the dominant surface — are covered.
  - **Vector C (MEDIUM, no silent loss):** no override token to a fitting type. `uint64` decimal path **FIXED** (`190ce50`), `datetime` token **FIXED** (`b8d7218`), `smallint`/`integer`/`int` tokens added for Vector D (v0.99.21). **embedded-NUL → PG text: FIXED v0.99.25** — a string carrying a NUL byte (`0x00`) bound for a PG `text`/`varchar`/`char` column is now refused loudly at `prepareValue` (`postgres/row_writer.go`) naming the column + the data-preserving remedy (`--type-override COL=bytea`), instead of pgx failing opaquely mid-COPY with SQLSTATE 22021 (a MySQL CHAR/VARCHAR/TEXT can hold embedded NULs; PG text cannot). No value silently altered (stripping the NUL would be silent corruption). Pinned `TestPrepareValueNULByteRefused` (text/varchar/char + DOMAIN-recursion + bytea-OK + NUL-free passthrough). **FIXED follow-ups:** (a) ✅ MySQL `TIME` duration (−838:59:59…838:59:59) → PG `INTERVAL` (v0.99.26) — new `ir.Interval` type (TierExtension) + `interval` override token; MySQL reads the column as its textual duration, PG emits `INTERVAL` and bulk-loads it via the batched-INSERT (text) path (pgx binary COPY can't encode a string→interval, so `tableHasIntervalColumn` routes it like the verbatim path); a MySQL/non-PG target refuses loudly (emitColumnType + `unsupportablePGtoMySQL`). Backup envelope round-trips it. Pinned end-to-end (838:59:59 / -12:30:00 / 00:00:05 → real PG interval, exact) + MySQL-target refusal. (b) ✅ `decimal(p,s)`/`numeric(p,s)`/`varchar(n)` paren CLI shorthand (v0.99.26) — and it turned out the old `decimal:precision=N,scale=M` hint **never parsed from the CLI** (only YAML `target_type_options`), so this is the first working CLI precision-bearing decimal; all the range-overflow advisories were corrected to the working `decimal(N,M)` form. Remaining Vector C: embedded-NUL **FIXED** (v0.99.25). Nothing left in Vector C except the broader Vector B silent-clamp gate (separate item below).
- **MySQL `BIGINT UNSIGNED` > 2^63−1 has NO working migration path to PG + the remediation hint is broken** (**FIXED `190ce50`, 2026-06-08** — `decodeDecimal`/`decodeString` carry uint64/int64 as exact text + the notice points at `--type-override COL=decimal:precision=20,scale=0`; unit + integration pinned). _(Original write-up retained for traceability.)_ Found 2026-06-08 on the v0.99.18 rig value-fidelity sweep. **No silent loss** — every path fails loud (exit≠0, 0 rows) — but it blocks a legitimate common migration (unsigned-64 IDs/counters/bitfields) and the *documented recovery path does not function*. Two confirmed defects: **(1) the MySQL value reader can't decode a `uint64` driver value for non-integer IR targets** — `decodeDecimal` (`value_decode.go:157`) and `decodeString` (`value_decode.go:181`) handle only `[]byte`/`string`, so `--type-override COL=decimal|text` fails `cannot decode uint64 as {Decimal|string}`; **(2) the unsigned-bigint notice's remediation is wrong** (`translate/unsigned_bigint.go:163` says `--type-override TABLE.COL=numeric`, but `numeric` is not a recognized override token — only `decimal` is — and `decimal` yields `numeric(10,0)`, too few digits for a 20-digit value). **Fix sketch:** add `uint64`/`int64` cases to `decodeDecimal`+`decodeString` (carry as exact decimal/text via `strconv.Format{Uint,Int}`); default an unsigned-64 `decimal` override to `numeric(20,0)` not `(10,0)`; correct the notice to name a token that exists *and* works end-to-end (or point at the YAML `mappings:` form if only YAML can set `numeric(20,0)` precision). **Pin:** MySQL→PG migrate of a `BIGINT UNSIGNED` column holding `2^64−1` must land the exact value via the documented override. Full write-up: rig `FINDING-uint64-no-migration-path.md` (2026-06-08).
- **NaN/±Inf refusal message has an empty `Examples: []` list** — ✅ **FIXED v0.99.28 (a bonus of the Vector B refactor).** Root cause: the LOAD-DATA-warning guard read `SELECT @@warning_count` BEFORE `SHOW WARNINGS`, and that intervening SELECT clears MySQL's diagnostic list, so `SHOW WARNINGS` returned nothing and `Examples` rendered empty. `reportBulkWriteWarnings` now reads `SHOW WARNINGS` first (one query → count + detail), so the refusal (NaN/±Inf and any other LOAD-DATA warning) names the offending values. (Found 2026-06-08 value-fidelity sweep probe #3.)

### Bug 27 (closed in v0.28.0)

Closed by ADR-0035 — VStream's `query.Type_GEOMETRY` cell decoder now strips the 4-byte little-endian SRID prefix before delivering bytes downstream, matching the vanilla MySQL driver path (`cdc_vstream.go:1354`). End-to-end verification runs against the local self-hosted Vitess cluster (`vitesscluster` build tag, roadmap item 1(e)): a `POINT` column is seeded, streamed via `FlavorVitess`, and the decoded WKB is asserted SRID-stripped against MySQL `ST_AsWKB`. This is the cheaper replacement for the originally-deferred `psverify` leg (no PlanetScale credentials required); the `psverify` spot-check remains available for operators who want to confirm against real hosted PlanetScale. See [ADR-0035](adr/adr-0035-postgis-geometry-spatial-support.md).

### Performance frontier (2026-06-12 profiling round — where the remaining time actually goes)

Two evidence rounds on v0.99.41-era main; profiles under `workspace/pprof-migrate-v09941/`
(gitignored), experiment logs in sluice-testing `workspace/perfB/`:

- **PG→PG migrate (raw-copy lane) is wire-bound, not compute-bound.** pprof on
  the 136 GB rig: sluice on-CPU ~6% of wall; the ADR-0078 passthrough does zero
  per-row work (0 flat samples in sluice functions; no steady-state allocs; no
  lock contention; `--table-parallelism=1` has the identical CPU shape). The
  only sluice-reducible item is the reader→writer `io.Pipe` memmove at <0.5% of
  wall. **Consequence: the positional-`ir.Row` rewrite (repo-audit P3) is NOT
  justified by this lane** — if it pays anywhere it's the cross-engine typed
  lane (TOAST/wide-row corpus differential is the test that would decide).
- **MySQL-target migrate sits at the InnoDB server floor.** sluice's LOAD DATA
  path (already 8-way parallel within-table via ADR-0019 chunking) matches a
  hand-run `LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE` to rig noise (~95k vs ~98k rows/s on the
  1M-row anchor); InnoDB single-table clustered-PK ingest does not parallelize
  (1×/4×/8× concurrent loaders all ≈100k) and is ingest-bound, not commit-bound
  (`innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit=2` ≈ +5%). **No Go-side or parallelism lever
  moves this number; myloader faces the same wall.** Per-direction tracking +
  the full numbers: sluice-testing `THROUGHPUT.md` (#34).
- **10k-tiny-tables (decides #56, measured 2026-06-12 — sluice-testing
  `workspace/perfC/VERDICTS.md`): sluice ≈13 ms/table vs pgcopydb ≈128 ms/table
  on the same corpus — sluice is ~10× AHEAD on this shape**, so the tiny-table
  batch lane is demand-gated, not perf-gated: do not build without a real user
  hitting it. The future lever, should demand appear, is precise: ~80% of wall
  is the serial CREATE TABLE phase (one network round-trip per table,
  `internal/engines/postgres/schema_writer.go:288-296`, flat across
  `--table-parallelism` which only governs bulk_copy) — a batch lane must
  batch DDL statements per round-trip, not COPY.
- **Wide-row typed lane (decides positional-`ir.Row`, audit P3 — same round):
  do NOT schedule the XL rewrite.** On a 750k × ~4.2 KB/row MySQL→PG copy
  (~200 MB/s, 8-way), the typed lane is 22.5% on-CPU and driver-dominated:
  pgx binary COPY-encode 42%, read/scan ~30%, sluice-owned typed-lane ~15% of
  which the `ir.Row` map cost (`copy_source.go:68` per-column lookup + value
  boxing) is ~8-9%. A perfect positional rewrite addresses single-digit CPU —
  far below the XL bar. Re-open only on separately-measured GC pressure at
  high concurrency.
- Remaining measured frontier worth a future chunk: backup-path zstd (32% of
  backup CPU post-codec — level sweep / parallel chunk compression).

### Connection-resilience + index-build tuning arc (2026-06-02; shipped across the v0.98.x arc)

Surfaced while building/load-testing the sluice-powered Heroku→PlanetScale migrator (`sluicesync/sluice-heroku-migrator`, a private fork of `planetscale/heroku-migrator` with the replication engine swapped from Bucardo to sluice's postgres-trigger engine). Validated end-to-end on real Heroku Postgres → PlanetScale; sluice's in-AWS throughput is ~18 MB/s same-region (the ~82 KB/s seen from a laptop was round-trip latency, not sluice — proven by `pg_dump|psql` matching it, and a ~118× speedup moving the work onto a dyno). Five chunks merged to `main`:

- **connection-resilience Phase 1** (`internal/engines/postgres/connect_appname.go`, `connection_budget.go`; `internal/pipeline/connection_budget.go`) — every PG connection now carries `application_name=sluice/<role>/<id>` (role-before-id so the prefix+role survive PG's 63-byte truncation); a target connection-budget preflight auto-caps parallel COPY to fit the slot budget and **refuses loudly** when `copy_budget < 1` (`--max-target-connections` override); PG connections adopt the `netkeepalive` dialer. Validated live (the `application_name` labels + a clean cross-region migration that previously failed on slot exhaustion).
- **connection-resilience Phase 2** (`internal/engines/postgres/stale_backend.go`) — cold-start preflight **detects** stale `sluice/%`-labeled, own-role, lock-holding/idle-in-tx backends and **reaps** them only with `--reap-stale-backends`. Terminate scoping is a single greppable constant; `pg_terminate_backend` sits in the SELECT projection (guaranteed scope-before-kill). The orphan-lockout failure mode (a SIGKILL'd COPY half-open, holding a target lock + a slot) is what this addresses. See [`docs/dev/notes/orphaned-backend-resilience.md`](notes/orphaned-backend-resilience.md).
- **connection-resilience Phase 2b** (`internal/pipeline/copy_backoff.go`, `copy_parallelism_gate.go`; `internal/engines/postgres/connection_slot.go`) — AIMD backoff on mid-copy `53300`/superuser-reserved-slots: multiplicative-decrease parallelism + retry the chunk rather than abort, with a bounded loud give-up. Classifier is narrowly scoped to `53300` (never masks a real error); retry is double-copy-safe because `53300` fails at connection-establishment, before any COPY write.
- **index-build tuning Phase A** (`internal/engines/postgres/index_build_tuning.go`; `CreateIndexes` refactor) — the dedicated index-build session SETs a `maintenance_work_mem` autotuned from `shared_buffers` (the clean RAM proxy; `RAM ≈ shared_buffers × 7`), pushing past the provider's ~4%-of-RAM steady-state default during the idle build phase (`--index-build-mem` override). Validated live: 16 MB → ~117 MB (**7.3×**) on a PlanetScale PS-5. See [`docs/dev/notes/index-build-phase-tuning.md`](notes/index-build-phase-tuning.md).
- **index-build tuning Phase B** — concurrent index builds via a bounded worker pool; N clamped by the connection budget, memory budget (**aggregate `N × per-build-mem ≤ budget`** — the OOM guard), and `--index-build-parallelism`. The note's tier data shows parallelism barely helps below PS-640 (`max_worker_processes` flat at 4), so auto-N stays conservative.

Also: the README + `docs/use-cases.md` "Heroku Postgres as a source" guidance was corrected (the postgres-trigger engine shipped — `--source-driver=postgres-trigger` + `--allow-polled-fingerprint` for Heroku's non-superuser role — it's no longer a "use Bucardo" gap). The backup gzip codec swapped stdlib `compress/gzip` → `klauspost/compress/gzip` (PR #142; the broader `--compression`/zstd-default work already shipped at v0.67.0, so roadmap item 7 Phase 2 is **done**, not pending). Open minor follow-ups: the Phase-2 reaper's exact-table (vs schema-scoped) lock heuristic if false positives ever appear; a deterministic 2b backoff-to-completion e2e.

### Silent-loss-class hardening + cross-engine DOMAIN closure arc (v0.93.0 → v0.97.1)

A push through the BUG-CATALOG.md backlog that took the open numbered-bug count from 8 to 0. Each release closed a numbered silent-loss class or operator-friction class; the v0.95.x → v0.97.x portion is the same Bug 113 family pursued from "loud refuse" → "round-trip carry" → "cross-engine WARN" → "cross-engine inline-CHECK enforcement on MySQL 8.0.16+" + strict-fidelity follow-up.

- **v0.93.0** — Bugs 112 + 119 + 120 (PG CDC schema-race silent drops on RENAME / DROP COLUMN / DROP+CREATE-same-name) closed via the `detectIncompatibleRelationChange` + `checkSchemaRace` RelationMessage-handler check at `internal/engines/postgres/cdc_relations.go`. Loud refusal with drained-model recovery hint; ADD COLUMN forwarding unaffected.
- **v0.94.0** — Bug 110 (incremental backup's end-position schema-read scope) closed via the `ir.TableScoper` predicate from the parent chain's recorded table set. An unrelated table carrying a verbatim-eligible type no longer breaks a chain originally scoped with `--include-table`.
- **v0.94.1** — Bug 117 verify-path closure (`VerifyBackupWith` + `probeChunkDecrypt`) + Bug 116 (manifest `FormatVersion=2` proportional version-stamp for RLS / Policies / EXCLUDE-bearing schemas). Older sluice restoring a newer-manifest chain now refuses loudly instead of silently dropping security metadata. Bug 118 re-verified closed in the same cycle.
- **v0.95.0** — Bug 115 (non-default core PG opclasses `text_pattern_ops` / `varchar_pattern_ops` / `jsonb_path_ops`) now carry through PG → PG via the `pg_opclass.opcdefault` reader branch.
- **v0.95.1** — Bug 113 loud-refuse: PG DOMAIN-typed columns refuse loudly at the read boundary instead of silently unwrapping to the base type. IR scaffolding (`ir.Domain`, `ir.DomainCheck`, `ir.ExtDomain`, JSON tagged-union round-trip) shipped here.
- **v0.95.2** — Bug 113 round-trip carry (schema half): PG schema reader populates `ir.Domain` from `pg_type` + `pg_constraint` joins; writer's Phase 1a' emits `CREATE DOMAIN` before tables.
- **v0.95.3** — Bug 122 closure (`ir.Domain` value codec dispatch in PG `decodeValue` + `prepareValue`, defense-in-depth MySQL `prepareValue` case). Unblocks Bug 113's row-data-carries outcome end-to-end on PG → PG.
- **v0.96.0** — Bug 108 (CLI-overrides-YAML on redaction rules) closed. `mergeYAMLRedactions` now checks `reg.Get` and skips YAML entries when a CLI `--redact` rule already exists, with a loud `slog.WARN` naming the displaced column + YAML strategy.
- **v0.96.1** — Bug 114 (PG migrate partial-failure leaves earlier tables without secondary indexes) closed via the `hints.go` PhaseBulkCopy registry entry. Loud abort now carries an actionable `hint:` line naming the missing-indexes state + the `--resume --exclude-table=<name>` recovery.
- **v0.96.2** — PG → MySQL DOMAIN-CHECK silent-downgrade WARN closed the residual cross-engine silent-loss carry-over from Bug 113. `maybeWarnDomainCheckDrop` emits one structured `slog.WARN` per writer lifetime carrying `affected_columns` / `source_domains` / `target_base_types` / `check_constraint_dropped` / actionable `hint`.
- **v0.96.3** — Bug 117 ingestion-path closure (symmetric to v0.94.1's verify-path closure). `IncrementalBackup.alignEncryption` + `BackupStream.alignEncryption` now probe the operator envelope against the parent's first per-chunk `WrappedCEK`; rotation surfaces at incremental start instead of at restore.
- **v0.97.0** — Bug 113 PG → MySQL inline-CHECK closure (Option A from the v0.96.x successor). MySQL 8.0.16+ targets get inline table-level CHECK clauses for the regex and range DOMAIN CHECK shapes — `VALUE ~ 'pattern'` → `REGEXP_LIKE(col, 'pattern')`, `VALUE >= X AND VALUE <= Y` → `col >= X AND col <= Y`. Version-gated via `SELECT VERSION()` probe; v0.96.2 WARN suppressed for fully-translated columns. Conservative whitelist; un-translatable shapes fall through to v0.96.2 WARN behavior.
- **v0.97.1** — PG → MySQL inline-CHECK regex backslash byte-fidelity follow-up. `translateRegexCheckBody` now doubles backslashes before quoting so MySQL's string-literal parser produces `\.` for the regex engine, not `.`. v0.97.0's `\.` → `.` collapse was functionally harmless on the email regex (the `@` carried the rejection) but the v0.97.0 cycle subagent flagged it as a strict-fidelity gap and this closes it.

Plus the docs layer that the arc unlocked:

- **v0.97.0 docs PR #131** — `docs/comparison-bucardo.md` (canonical OSS PG → PG head-to-head with corrected default-config latency framing) + `docs/cookbook/` scaffolding (4 recipes + GitLab case study).
- **v0.97.1 docs ride-along** — 3 more cookbook recipes (`compare-pg-dump.md`, `recipe-heroku-migration.md`, `recipe-postgis.md`) bringing the cookbook to 8 entries.

End-of-arc state: 0 numbered bugs open; 0 tracked silent-loss-class follow-ups. Roadmap "Next up" items 11 (Tier 3 ext fn-defaults), 13 (view Phase 3), 15c (JSON-path redaction), and 18 sub-bullets beyond ADR-0068 remain as the demand-gated forward-looking pieces.

### Bulk-copy throughput arc — ADR-0042 / ADR-0043 (v0.62.0 → v0.64.0)

- **v0.62.0 — `--bulk-parallel-min-rows` default 100,000 → 80,000.** Absorbs the typical InnoDB `table_rows` catalog undershoot so 100k-actual tables consistently engage parallel-copy by default. `defaultBulkParallelMinRows` constant change; explicit-value behaviour unchanged.
- **ADR-0042 — MySQL bulk-copy throughput investigation.** Accepted as a discovery doc; Phase A added DEBUG-gated per-chunk `adr0042:` instrumentation (retained as a permanent diagnostic artifact, like the ADR-0033/0036 verify probes).
- **v0.63.1 — finding N1: PG cold-start parallel-copy fix.** `internal/engines/postgres` `CountRows` falls back to exact `SELECT COUNT(*)` when `pg_class.reltuples` is the never-analyzed sentinel (`-1`/`0`), so freshly loaded/restored PG sources no longer silently single-thread. PG-specific/asymmetric (MySQL's `information_schema.tables.table_rows` is InnoDB-populated on load). Biggest impact PG → MySQL.
- **v0.64.0 — ADR-0043: native fast loader on the cold-start parallel-copy path.** The parallel chunk writer is now situation-driven (no new flag): a fresh cold-start chunk into a proven-empty target streams through one native `COPY`/`LOAD DATA` call; resume / `--force-cold-start` / live-add stay on the idempotent upsert path. Four-gate rule; crash-safe (next invocation is a resume → idempotent replay). MySQL → MySQL medium fixture ~31s → ~24s wall; PG → PG no regression (schema/DDL-bound — ADR-0042 finding N2). Pinned by a permanent both-engines proof-of-falsification integration test.

### PII redaction track — Phases 1 → 4 complete (v0.53.0 → v0.63.0)

- **Phase 1 + 1.5 (v0.53.0–v0.55.0).** `--redact TABLE.COLUMN=STRATEGY[:options]` + YAML `redactions:`; `null` / `static` / `hash:sha256` / `hash:hmac-sha256` / `truncate`; `internal/redact` package; per-bulk-copy-variant wiring; audit log line. Phase 1.5 closed CDC apply-path redaction + schema-preview annotation + backup-stream redaction. Bug 58 (CDC schema-namespace key mismatch) v0.54.1; Bug 59 (kong comma-split) v0.56.1.
- **Phase 2 (v0.56.0–v0.60.0).** Phase 2.a generic `mask:inner`/`mask:outer` + Luhn helper; Phase 2.b mask presets (ssn/pan/pan-relaxed/email/ca-sin/uk-nin/iban/uuid; Bug 60 `mask:uuid` preflight v0.58.1); Phase 2.c replay-stable `randomize:*` generators (ADR-0039 per-row seed contract).
- **Phase 3 (v0.61.0).** Dictionary strategies `randomize:dict` (PK-keyed) + `tokenize:dict` (input-value-keyed) + YAML `dictionaries:` block. ADR-0040 documents the two determinism contracts.
